definition_zh: 欺诈；诈骗；骗子；骗局；假冒之物
definition_en: the crime of deceiving people in order to get money or something else of value
core_image: 一张伪造的签名在灯下几乎看不出破绽
scene: 古董店里，买家发现所谓的名家字画其实是复制品。The buyer realized that the painting was a fraud sold as an original.
sceneCN: 这里 fraud 是「骗局、假冒之物」（第 3 个义项：被当作真品呈现的虚假事物）；句意：买家发现那幅画是当作真迹出售的假货。

pos.zh: 欺诈；诈骗；骗子；骗局；假冒之物

derivatives.zh: 由 fraud 加拉丁形容词后缀 -ulent 构成，指欺诈的、骗人的
由 fraud 加指人后缀 -ster 构成，指骗子、行骗者
由 fraudulent 加后缀 -ence 构成，指欺诈性、虚假
由前缀 de- 加 fraud 构成，指诈骗他人钱财

senses.title: The act of deceiving for gain
senses.definition: the act of tricking people in order to get money or property
senses.definitionCN: 为获取钱财或财物而欺骗他人
senses.example: He was jailed for committing fraud.
senses.exampleCN: 他因实施诈骗而入狱。
senses.why: Latin fraus means deceit or injury, so the act sense is the oldest one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 fraus 意为「欺骗、损害」，所以「行为」义是最古老的义项。

senses.title: A person who deceives
senses.definition: someone who pretends to be something they are not in order to cheat others
senses.definitionCN: 为欺骗他人而冒充某种身份的人
senses.example: The man who sold the shares was a fraud.
senses.exampleCN: 卖股票的那个人是个骗子。
senses.why: A deed of deceit easily shifts to the doer, by the usual pattern of naming a person after the act.
senses.whyCN: 欺骗行为很容易按「以行为指人」的常见模式转到行骗者身上。

senses.title: A fake thing or scheme
senses.definition: something false that is presented as genuine
senses.definitionCN: 被当作真品呈现的虚假事物
senses.example: The antique dealer sold him a fraud.
senses.exampleCN: 古董商卖给他一件假货。
senses.why: If an act of deceit can become a thing, then any object built to deceive carries the same name.
senses.whyCN: 既然欺骗行为可以变成一件「事」，那么任何为骗人而造的东西也能叫这个名字。

senses.title: The legal wrong of deception
senses.definition: a civil or criminal wrong based on deliberate deception
senses.definitionCN: 以故意欺骗为基础的民事或刑事违法行为
senses.example: The company faced charges of fraud.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司面临欺诈指控。
senses.why: Law turned the general deceit into a named wrong with its own rules of proof.
senses.whyCN: 法律把一般的欺骗固定为一种有独立举证规则的违法行为。

intro.en: Fraud comes from Latin fraus, deceit, whose stem fraud- passes through Old French fraude into English.
intro.cn: fraud 来自拉丁语 fraus（欺骗），其词干 fraud- 经古法语 fraude 进入英语。

items.en: Fraus means deceit, trickery, or injury.
items.cn: fraus 意为欺骗、诡计或损害。

items.en: The stem fraud- appears in the genitive form fraudis.
items.cn: 词干 fraud- 出现在属格形式 fraudis 中。

items.en: Old French fraude keeps the legal sense of deceit.
items.cn: 古法语 fraude 保留了「欺骗」的法律含义。

items.en: Middle English fraud names deception and the profit it brings.
items.cn: 中古英语 fraud 指欺骗以及由此得来的利益。

items.en: Modern English adds the person, the fake object, and the legal charge.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了行骗者、假冒之物与法律罪名。

note.en: Fraud is the noun of deceit, surrounded by its adjective, its person noun, and the verb defraud.
note.cn: fraud 是表示「欺骗」的名词，周围有它的形容词、指人的名词以及动词 defraud。

entries.definition: dishonest and intended to deceive
entries.definitionCN: 欺诈的；骗人的

entries.definition: someone who commits fraud
entries.definitionCN: 骗子；行骗者

entries.definition: to cheat someone out of money
entries.definitionCN: 诈骗他人的钱财

entries.definition: a lie or trick used to mislead someone
entries.definitionCN: 欺骗；谎言

entries.definition: a dishonest scheme for taking money
entries.definitionCN: 骗取钱财的骗局

entries.definition: to cheat someone out of money by a trick
entries.definitionCN: 以花招诈骗钱财

normalIntro.en: Fraud is deceit with a profit: every sense grows from a trick played for gain.
normalIntro.cn: fraud 是带着利益的欺骗：每个义项都从「为获利而设的骗局」长出来。

normal.en: Commit fraud is the standard verb phrase for this crime.
normal.cn: commit fraud 是表示这项罪行的标准动宾搭配。

normal.en: A tax fraud case can end in prison.
normal.cn: 税务欺诈案可能以入狱告终。

normal.en: A fraud can be a person as well as an act.
normal.cn: fraud 既可以指行为，也可以指人。

normal.en: The adjective fraudulent describes documents and claims.
normal.cn: 形容词 fraudulent 用来形容文件与说法。

normal.en: Compare scam: scam is informal, while fraud is the legal and general word.
normal.cn: 对比 scam：scam 更口语，fraud 是法律与通用说法。

abstract.en: Picture a forged signature drying on a cheque.
abstract.cn: 想象伪造的签名在支票上慢慢干透。

abstract.en: Imagine a man wearing a uniform he never earned.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人穿着他从未获得的制服。

abstract.en: Think of a gold watch that leaves green marks on your wrist.
abstract.cn: 想象一块金表在你手腕上留下绿痕。

examples.en: She was found guilty of fraud after the audit.
examples.cn: 审计之后，她被判欺诈罪名成立。

examples.en: The so-called expert turned out to be a fraud.
examples.cn: 那位所谓的专家原来是个骗子。

examples.en: Banks spend millions detecting credit card frauds.
examples.cn: 银行花费数百万侦测信用卡诈骗。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗洛德」——谐音「糊弄的」，糊弄别人骗取钱财就是欺诈；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 fraus（欺骗、损害）→ 词干 fraud- → 古法语 fraude → 中古英语 fraud → 现代英语 fraud，核心义「以假取利」。

sensesIntro.en: Fraud begins with the act of deception, then names the deceiver, the fake thing, and finally the legal charge.
sensesIntro.cn: fraud 从欺骗行为开始，随后指行骗者、假冒之物，最后固定为法律罪名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a forged signature that looks almost real.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个几乎看不出破绽的伪造签名。

branches.en: The act of deception is the root sense.
branches.cn: 欺骗行为是最根本的义项。

branches.en: The doer takes the name of the deed.
branches.cn: 行骗者直接借用了行为之名。

branches.en: A thing made to deceive is called by the same word.
branches.cn: 为骗人而造的东西也用同一个词来称呼。

branches.en: Law gives the deceit a formal name and a penalty.
branches.cn: 法律给这种欺骗一个正式名称与惩罚。

branches.en: One who commits fraud is named by the very act.
branches.cn: 实施欺诈的人直接用这一行为来命名。

intro.en: Fraud is a Latin deceit noun; English builds fraudulent, fraudster, and defraud around the same stem.
intro.cn: fraud 是拉丁语中表示「欺骗」的名词，英语围绕同一词干构成 fraudulent、fraudster 与 defraud。

latinIntro.en: Latin fraus means deceit, and its stem fraud- carries the word into French and English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fraus 意为欺骗，其词干 fraud- 把这个词带入法语与英语。

items.example: Fraus is the source noun.
items.exampleCN: fraus 是来源名词。

items.example: Fraudis supplies the stem fraud-.
items.exampleCN: fraudis 提供词干 fraud-。

items.example: Latin fraudare means to cheat someone.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 fraudare 意为欺骗某人。

items.example: Old French fraude keeps the noun.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 fraude 保留了这个名词。

items.example: English fraud keeps the legal sense.
items.exampleCN: 英语 fraud 保留了法律含义。

items.example: Latin fraudulentus gives the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 fraudulentus 提供形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ulent forms fraudulent.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ulent 构成 fraudulent。

items.example: The suffix -ster forms fraudster.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ster 构成 fraudster。

items.example: The prefix de- forms defraud.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 de- 构成 defraud。

items.example: Defraud adds the prefix to fraud.
items.exampleCN: defraud 在 fraud 前加了前缀。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ence forms fraudulence.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ence 构成 fraudulence。

definition_zh: 充满…的；伴随…的；焦虑不安的；满载的
definition_en: full of something unpleasant, such as danger, difficulty, or strong emotion
core_image: 一条满载的船被货物压得吃水很深，在浪里吱呀作响
scene: 谈判桌上，双方都沉默着，气氛紧得让人不敢呼吸。The silence in the room was fraught with tension.
sceneCN: 这里 fraught 是「充满（紧张情绪）的」（第 1 个义项：带有强烈的危险、困难或风险成分）；句意：房间里的沉默充满了紧张。

pos.zh: 充满…的；焦虑不安的；满载的

derivatives.zh: 由 fraught 加后缀 -ness 构成，指焦虑、充满紧张的状态
与 fraught 同出中古荷兰语 vracht 的同源双式词，指货物、运费

senses.title: Full of something bad
senses.definition: carrying a strong element of danger, difficulty, or risk
senses.definitionCN: 带有强烈的危险、困难或风险成分
senses.example: The journey was fraught with danger.
senses.exampleCN: 这段旅程充满危险。
senses.why: The word began as a past participle meaning loaded, and a loaded ship is full of cargo.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是意为「装载」的过去分词，装满的船自然「充满」货物。

senses.title: Anxious and tense
senses.definition: nervous, worried, and unable to relax
senses.definitionCN: 紧张、担忧而无法放松
senses.example: She felt fraught before the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 面试前她感到焦虑不安。
senses.why: A loaded rope or ship is under strain, so the sense of being weighed down turns into personal tension.
senses.whyCN: 满载的缆绳或船承受着拉力，于是「被重压」的感觉转为人的精神紧张。

senses.title: Loaded or carrying a burden
senses.definition: carrying a load, especially on a ship
senses.definitionCN: 承载着货物，尤指船上装载
senses.example: The old ship was fraught with grain.
senses.exampleCN: 那艘旧船上满载着谷物。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, kept in literary use after the everyday loading verb faded.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，在表示「装载」的日常动词消失后仍保留于书面语。

senses.title: Charged with strong feeling
senses.definition: full of emotion or meaning that is easy to sense
senses.definitionCN: 充满容易被感受到的情绪或意味
senses.example: Her words were fraught with meaning.
senses.exampleCN: 她的话意味深长。
senses.why: Once fraught with could mean full of anything, emotion became one of its favourite fillings.
senses.whyCN: 当 fraught with 可以指「充满任何事物」之后，情感成了它最常用的填充物。

intro.en: Fraught began as the past participle of a loading verb, from Middle Dutch vracht, cargo; it is a doublet of freight.
intro.cn: fraught 最初是表示「装载」的动词的过去分词，来自中古荷兰语 vracht（货物）；它与 freight 是同源双式词。

items.en: Vracht, also written vrecht, means cargo or freight.
items.cn: vracht（也写作 vrecht）意为货物、运费。

items.en: Middle English fraught is the past participle of fraughten, to load a ship.
items.cn: 中古英语 fraught 是 fraughten（装船）的过去分词。

items.en: The phrase fraught with moves from cargo to any kind of burden.
items.cn: 短语 fraught with 从货物扩展到任何一种负担。

items.en: Writers begin to use fraught for situations full of danger or difficulty.
items.cn: 作家开始用 fraught 形容充满危险或困难的处境。

items.en: Modern English adds the emotional sense of being tense and anxious.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「紧张、焦虑」的情感义。

note.en: Fraught is the loaded adjective, a doublet of freight and a near neighbour of words for tension.
note.cn: fraught 是表示「承载」的形容词，与 freight 同源，并与表示紧张的一类词相邻。

entries.definition: goods carried by ship, train, or truck
entries.definitionCN: 货物；运费（与 fraught 同源的双式词）

entries.definition: sudden fear
entries.definitionCN: 惊恐（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a current of air, or a drink drawn from a container
entries.definitionCN: 气流；散装饮品（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: carrying a heavy load
entries.definitionCN: 满载的；负重前行的

entries.definition: nervous and unable to relax
entries.definitionCN: 紧张的；绷紧的

entries.definition: full of strong emotion or meaning
entries.definitionCN: 充满强烈情绪或意味的

normalIntro.en: Fraught is a cargo word turned feeling word: what is loaded can be dangerous, and danger makes people tense.
normalIntro.cn: fraught 是从「货物」转向「感受」的词：装得太满会危险，而危险让人紧张。

normal.en: Fraught with danger means full of danger.
normal.cn: fraught with danger 意为充满危险。

normal.en: A fraught silence is a tense silence.
normal.cn: a fraught silence 指令人紧张的沉默。

normal.en: Freight and fraught come from the same Dutch cargo word.
normal.cn: freight 与 fraught 来自同一个荷兰语「货物」词。

normal.en: The phrase fraught with is the most common pattern.
normal.cn: 短语 fraught with 是最常见的搭配。

normal.en: Compare tense: fraught adds the idea of being loaded with something.
normal.cn: 对比 tense：fraught 多了「被某种东西装满」的意思。

abstract.en: Picture a small boat riding low under too many crates.
abstract.cn: 想象一条小船被太多木箱压得吃水很深。

abstract.en: Imagine a rope pulled so tight that it hums.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子被拉得发出嗡鸣。

abstract.en: Think of a cart piled higher than the driver can see past.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆堆得比车夫视线还高的马车。

examples.en: The rescue attempt was fraught with danger.
examples.cn: 这次营救行动充满危险。

examples.en: The weeks before the wedding were fraught and sleepless.
examples.cn: 婚礼前的几周紧张而失眠。

examples.en: Every message from the front was fraught with meaning.
examples.cn: 前线的每一条消息都意味深长。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗洛特」——谐音「浮着太多」，船浮着太多货物，引申为充满、紧绷；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 中古荷兰语 vracht（货物、运费）→ 中古英语 fraughten（装载）→ fraught（满载的）→ fraught with（充满…）→ 现代英语「焦虑的」，核心义「被装满」。

sensesIntro.en: Fraught moves from a ship loaded with cargo to any situation loaded with danger, then to the tension such a load creates, and finally to charged emotion.
sensesIntro.cn: fraught 从装满货物的船，走到充满危险的处境，再走到这种重压造成的紧张，最后指充满情感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boat sitting low under a heavy load.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条被重货压得吃水很低的船。

branches.en: Being full of danger grows from being full of cargo.
branches.cn: 「充满危险」是从「装满货物」长出来的。

branches.en: Strain on the load becomes strain in the mind.
branches.cn: 货物承受的拉力变成了心里的紧绷。

branches.en: The oldest loading sense survives in literary use.
branches.cn: 最古老的「装载」义仍保留在书面语中。

branches.en: Emotion is one more thing a situation can be full of.
branches.cn: 情感只是处境可以「装满」的又一种东西。

branches.en: Both senses describe a container filled to its limit, with danger or with feeling.
branches.cn: 这两个义项都指容器被装到极限，装的可以是危险，也可以是情感。

intro.en: Fraught is a Germanic cargo word with no Latin root; English relatives include freight and the suffix -ness in fraughtness.
intro.cn: fraught 是日耳曼语系的「货物」词，没有拉丁词根；英语亲属词包括 freight，以及构成 fraughtness 的后缀 -ness。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor here: fraught and freight both come from Middle Dutch vracht.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语祖先：fraught 与 freight 都来自中古荷兰语 vracht。

items.example: Vracht is the source word.
items.exampleCN: vracht 是来源词。

items.example: Vrecht is a variant form.
items.exampleCN: vrecht 是变体形式。

items.example: Fraughten is the loading verb.
items.exampleCN: fraughten 是表示装载的动词。

items.example: Fraught keeps the participle sense.
items.exampleCN: fraught 保留了分词含义。

items.example: The phrase extends the load image.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语延伸了「装载」意象。

items.example: Freight is the doublet of fraught.
items.exampleCN: freight 是 fraught 的同源双式词。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms fraughtness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 fraughtness。

items.example: Fraughtness names the state.
items.exampleCN: fraughtness 指这种状态。

items.example: Freightage adds the -age suffix.
items.exampleCN: freightage 加了后缀 -age。

definition_zh: 狂乱的；发狂似的；极度忙乱的
definition_en: wildly excited, fast, and lacking calm control
core_image: 一台转得飞快的机器，齿轮空转、火花四溅，人追着它手忙脚乱
scene: 舞台上的鼓点越敲越快，舞者的动作几乎失去控制。The drums grew louder and the dancers moved at a frenetic pace across the stage.
sceneCN: 这里 frenetic 是「狂乱的、高速而失控的」（第 1 个义项：兴奋到失去常态）；句意：鼓声越来越响，舞者以狂乱的节奏穿过舞台。

pos.zh: 狂乱的；发狂似的；极度忙乱的

collocations.zh: 狂乱的节奏；飞快的步调

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ally 构成，义为「狂乱地；拼命地」
同一希腊词根的异形词，义为「发狂似的；慌乱不堪的」

senses.title: Wildly excited and uncontrolled
senses.definition: wildly excited and behaving without calm control
senses.definitionCN: 极度兴奋，行为失去冷静的控制
senses.example: The fans gave a frenetic welcome to the band.
senses.exampleCN: 歌迷们以近乎狂乱的方式欢迎乐队。
senses.why: Greek phrēn meant the mind, and a fever of the mind was pictured as wild, uncontrolled behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 phrēn 指「心智」，心智发烧时人就会狂乱失控；这个词的起点正是「心智发热」这幅画面。

senses.title: Moving at great speed
senses.definition: very fast and busy, so that everything seems rushed
senses.definitionCN: 极快且忙碌，一切都像被赶着走
senses.example: The kitchen was frenetic just before the dinner service.
senses.exampleCN: 晚餐开席前，厨房里一片忙乱。
senses.why: Inner fever shows on the outside as speed, so the word came to describe action that races ahead of calm.
senses.whyCN: 内心的「发热」表现在外就是速度，于是这个词用来形容抢在冷静之前的动作。

senses.title: Feverishly enthusiastic
senses.definition: showing intense, almost feverish enthusiasm for something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事表现出强烈到近乎发烧的热情
senses.example: She made a frenetic effort to finish the painting.
senses.exampleCN: 她以近乎狂热的劲头赶完了那幅画。
senses.why: The heat of the original fever survives here as burning enthusiasm.
senses.whyCN: 最初「发烧」的热度在这里留下痕迹，变成了灼热的热情。

senses.title: Delirious in the old medical sense
senses.definition: suffering from delirium, in the older medical use of the word
senses.definitionCN: 按较早的医学用法，指处于谵妄状态
senses.example: Old medical texts describe a frenetic patient raving in bed.
senses.exampleCN: 旧医学文献描述谵妄的病人躺在床上说胡话。
senses.why: The word entered English as the name of a brain fever, so this delirious sense is the oldest layer.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初进入英语时就是「脑热病」的名称，所以谵妄一义是最古老的一层。

senses.title: Fast and frantic in rhythm
senses.definition: of music or movement, very fast and seemingly out of control
senses.definitionCN: 指音乐或动作极快，听起来像失去控制
senses.example: The set ended with a frenetic drum solo.
senses.exampleCN: 演出以一段急促的鼓独奏结束。
senses.why: Music makes the inner fever audible: a tempo so quick that it sounds uncontrolled.
senses.whyCN: 音乐让内在的「发热」变得可听：节拍快到听上去已经失控。

senses.title: Feverish in markets and competition
senses.definition: describing trade, competition, or demand that is intense and hard to control
senses.definitionCN: 形容交易、竞争或需求极其激烈而难以控制
senses.example: Trading on the exchange turned frenetic at midday.
senses.exampleCN: 中午时分，交易所里的交易变得近乎疯狂。
senses.why: Crowds and markets can run a fever too, so the word extends from one mind to many.
senses.whyCN: 人群与市场也会「发烧」，于是这个词从一个人的心智扩展到许多人的集体行为。

senses.title: Hurried and clumsy
senses.definition: so hurried that movements become clumsy and disorganized
senses.definitionCN: 匆忙到动作变得笨拙而混乱
senses.example: He made a frenetic attempt to catch the falling cups.
senses.exampleCN: 他手忙脚乱地想去接住掉下来的杯子。
senses.why: Speed without control looks clumsy, which is the practical face of the same wild energy.
senses.whyCN: 没有控制的快速看上去就是笨拙，这是同一种狂乱能量在生活里的实际样子。

senses.title: Wild with anger
senses.definition: wildly angry and unable to restrain oneself
senses.definitionCN: 暴怒而无法约束自己
senses.example: Her frenetic shouting drove the neighbours indoors.
senses.exampleCN: 她狂怒的喊叫把邻居都逼回了屋里。
senses.why: The same loss of mental control can turn from excitement into rage, so the word covers anger too.
senses.whyCN: 同一种心智失控也可以从兴奋转为暴怒，所以这个词也能形容愤怒。

normalIntro.en: Frenetic is a fever word: think first of a mind running too hot, then of hands moving too fast.
normalIntro.cn: frenetic 是一个「发热」词：先想到过热的心智，再想到过快的手脚。

normal.en: Frenetic activity is busy in a disordered, almost mad way.
normal.cn: frenetic activity 指的是一种近乎发疯的忙乱活动。

normal.en: A frenetic pace is faster and less controlled than a busy pace.
normal.cn: frenetic pace 比 busy pace 更快、更失控。

normal.en: The adverb frenetically describes doing something at top speed.
normal.cn: 副词 frenetically 表示以最高速度做事。

normal.en: Frantic is the plainer twin of frenetic, used more for worry and fear.
normal.cn: frantic 是 frenetic 更朴素的同源词，多用于担忧与恐惧。

normal.en: Frenzy is the matching noun: the state behind frenetic behaviour.
normal.cn: frenzy 是相配的名词，指 frenetic 行为背后的那种状态。

abstract.en: Picture a spinning top that cannot stop and starts to wobble.

abstract.en: Imagine a chef juggling four pans over one flame.
abstract.cn: 想象一位厨师在一个灶火上同时抛翻四只锅。

abstract.en: Think of a fever chart climbing off the top of the page.
abstract.cn: 想象一张体温曲线冲出纸面顶端。

examples.en: The city runs at a frenetic pace that leaves visitors breathless.
examples.cn: 这座城市以狂乱的节奏运转，让游客喘不过气。

examples.en: He worked frenetically through the night to meet the deadline.
examples.cn: 为了赶上截止时间，他整夜拼命工作。

examples.en: The crowd became frenetic when the singer appeared.
examples.cn: 歌手一出现，人群就陷入狂乱。

sensesIntro.en: Frenetic begins as a medical word for a fevered mind, then spreads to wild excitement, to speed, and finally to clumsy haste and anger.

branches.en: Wild excitement is the layer closest to the original fever.
branches.cn: 狂乱的兴奋是最接近最初「发热」意象的一层。

branches.en: Speed is how the inner fever shows on the outside.
branches.cn: 速度是内心发热在外表上的显现。

branches.en: Enthusiasm borrows the heat of the fever image.
branches.cn: 狂热投入借用的是「发热」意象里的热度。

branches.en: Wild energy and clumsy haste are the same motion seen from inside and outside.
branches.cn: 狂乱的能量与手忙脚乱是同一种动作从内外两侧看到的样子。

branches.en: Delirium and rage are the two extremes of a mind that has lost control.
branches.cn: 谵妄与狂怒是心智失控的两个极端。

definition_en: a state of wild excitement or anger that is hard to control
core_image: 一口烧得过旺的锅，锅盖被蒸汽顶得上下跳动
scene: 球赛结束后，整条街都被欢呼声淹没。The whole street was in a frenzy after the final whistle.
sceneCN: 这里 frenzy 是「群体性的狂热兴奋」（第 4 个义项：在人群中迅速扩散的兴奋）；句意：终场哨响后，整条街都陷入狂热。

pos.zh: 狂乱；狂热；暴怒；骚动

derivatives.zh: 由名词加 -ed 构成，义为「狂乱的；疯狂的」
由 frenzied 加 -ly 构成，义为「狂乱地」

senses.title: Wild excitement
senses.definition: a state of wild excitement that is hard to control
senses.definitionCN: 难以控制的极度兴奋状态
senses.example: The crowd was in a frenzy as the gates opened.
senses.exampleCN: 大门打开时，人群陷入狂乱。
senses.why: The Greek source names a fever of the mind, and frenzy keeps that image of heat without control.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语源头指「心智发烧」，frenzy 保留了这幅「热而失控」的画面。

senses.title: Wild rage
senses.definition: a state of violent anger that cannot be restrained
senses.definitionCN: 无法抑制的暴烈愤怒状态
senses.example: He smashed the phone in a frenzy of rage.
senses.exampleCN: 他在一阵暴怒中把手机摔碎了。
senses.why: The same heat can burn as anger instead of joy, so frenzy covers rage.
senses.whyCN: 同一股「热」也可以烧成愤怒而不是欢喜，所以 frenzy 也能指暴怒。

senses.title: Feverish activity
senses.definition: intense, hurried activity that seems beyond control
senses.definitionCN: 强烈而匆忙、似乎已失控的活动
senses.example: The office worked in a frenzy to finish the report.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室里的人疯狂赶工，想把报告做完。
senses.why: Fever drives the body to move fast, so the noun shifts from feeling to frantic doing.
senses.whyCN: 发烧使身体动作变快，于是这个名词从感受转到近乎失控的忙碌。

senses.title: Contagious group excitement
senses.definition: excitement that spreads quickly through a crowd
senses.definitionCN: 在人群中迅速扩散的兴奋
senses.example: A frenzy spread through the stadium after the goal.
senses.exampleCN: 进球之后，一阵狂热席卷了整个体育场。
senses.why: Heat spreads, and so does excitement, which is why frenzy describes crowds so often.
senses.whyCN: 热会扩散，兴奋也会扩散，所以 frenzy 常用来描述人群。

senses.title: A craze for buying or following
senses.definition: a sudden intense demand for a product or a person
senses.definitionCN: 对某件商品或某个人突然产生的强烈追捧
senses.example: The new phone caused a buying frenzy in the first hour.
senses.exampleCN: 新手机开卖第一个小时就引发了抢购热潮。
senses.why: A crowd in heat turns into a market in heat, chasing the same object.
senses.whyCN: 发热的人群会变成发热的市场，一起追同一个东西。

senses.title: Tumult and disorder
senses.definition: a state of noisy disorder and agitated movement
senses.definitionCN: 喧闹混乱、到处躁动的状态
senses.example: The square was a frenzy of horns and shouting.
senses.exampleCN: 广场上喇叭与喊叫声混成一片骚动。
senses.why: When many excited bodies move at once, the result is audible disorder.
senses.whyCN: 许多兴奋的身体同时移动，结果就是听得见的混乱。

senses.title: A fit of madness
senses.definition: a short period of madness or delirium
senses.definitionCN: 短时间的精神失常或谵妄
senses.example: In his frenzy he did not recognise his own house.
senses.exampleCN: 他在神志失常中连自己的房子都认不出来。
senses.why: The oldest medical sense survives as a name for a temporary loss of reason.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的医学义项留下来，用来指理智的短暂丧失。

senses.title: A violent burst of feeling
senses.definition: a sudden uncontrolled outburst of emotion such as grief or joy
senses.definitionCN: 悲喜等情感突然而失控的爆发
senses.example: She wept in a frenzy of grief at the grave.
senses.exampleCN: 她在墓前悲恸得失声痛哭。
senses.why: Any strong feeling can run hot enough to be called a frenzy.
senses.whyCN: 任何强烈的感情都可能热到被称为 frenzy。

examples.cn: 婚礼消息公布后，媒体陷入一片狂热。

definition_en: to worry continuously, or to wear something away slowly
core_image: 一根手指反复摩挲桌面同一处，把漆面磨出浅浅的痕
scene: 她整个星期都在为面试坐立不安。She frets about the interview all week.
sceneCN: 这里 fret 是「持续担心、坐立不安」（第 1 个义项：长时间反复忧虑）；句意：她整个星期都为面试焦虑。

pos.zh: 焦虑；发愁；烦躁

senses.title: To worry continuously
senses.definition: to worry about something over a long period
senses.definitionCN: 长时间地为某事忧虑
senses.example: She frets about her son every time he travels.
senses.exampleCN: 儿子每次出门，她都会为他担心。
senses.why: Old English fretan meant to eat away, and worry was pictured as something eating at the mind.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 fretan 意为「啃食掉」，忧虑被想象成有东西在一点点啃食心智，这正是持续焦虑的画面。

senses.title: To worry over small matters
senses.definition: to be troubled by small, everyday details
senses.definitionCN: 被日常小事困扰
senses.example: He frets over every scratch on the car.
senses.exampleCN: 车上每道划痕都让他心烦。
senses.why: The gnawing image shrinks to small bites, which is how the word came to mean fussing over trifles.
senses.whyCN: 「啃食」的画面缩小成一小口一小口，这个词于是用来指为琐事反复计较。

senses.title: To make someone anxious
senses.definition: to cause someone to feel restless or anxious
senses.definitionCN: 使某人感到不安或烦躁
senses.example: The constant noise frets the whole family.
senses.exampleCN: 持续的噪音让全家人都烦躁不安。
senses.why: The verb turns outward: what gnaws at a person is felt as an irritation coming from outside.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词转向外部：啃食人的东西被感受为来自外界的刺激，于是有了「使人烦躁」的用法。

senses.title: To complain with agitation
senses.definition: to complain or grumble in a restless, agitated way
senses.definitionCN: 烦躁不安地抱怨、发牢骚
senses.example: The old man fretted about the weather for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 老人为天气的事絮絮叨叨抱怨了一个小时。
senses.why: Worry that cannot stay inside comes out as complaint, so the word also names grumbling.
senses.whyCN: 留不住的忧虑会变成抱怨流出来，所以这个词也指发牢骚。

senses.title: To eat away or corrode
senses.definition: to wear something away gradually, as if by eating into it
senses.definitionCN: 像啃食一样逐渐磨损某物
senses.example: Salt air frets the iron railings by the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 海边的盐雾侵蚀着铁栏杆。
senses.why: This is the oldest physical sense: the word literally meant to devour or gnaw.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的物理义项：这个词本义就是吞食、啃咬。

senses.title: To chafe the skin
senses.definition: to rub against something and slowly make it sore
senses.definitionCN: 反复摩擦而使某处疼痛
senses.example: The strap frets the skin on his shoulder.
senses.exampleCN: 带子把他肩上的皮肤磨疼了。
senses.why: Gnawing became rubbing: repeated contact wears a surface down, whether metal or skin.
senses.whyCN: 啃食变成了摩擦：反复接触会把表面磨掉，金属如此，皮肤也如此。

senses.title: A state of agitation
senses.definition: a state of restless anxiety or irritation
senses.definitionCN: 烦躁不安、心神不宁的状态
senses.example: He has been in a fret since the letter arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 信到了以后，他一直心神不宁。
senses.why: English lets the verb become a noun, so the gnawing can be named as a state a person is in.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许动词转成名词，于是这种「被啃食」的感觉可以被命名为人所处的状态。

senses.title: A bout of visible worry
senses.definition: a short period of worrying shown in behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 短暂表现在行为上的担心与烦躁
senses.example: Her evening fret lasted until the phone rang.
senses.exampleCN: 她晚上那阵烦躁一直持续到电话响起。
senses.why: The same noun can count one episode, which is why the plural frets names repeated bouts.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也可以计量一次发作，所以复数 frets 指一回又一回的烦躁。

intro.en: Fret is a Germanic word: Old English fretan meant to devour, and worry grew out of the image of being eaten away.
intro.cn: fret 是日耳曼语词：古英语 fretan 意为吞食，「忧虑」义从「被一点点啃食」的画面里长出来。

items.en: A reconstructed root for eating is thought to lie behind the word.
items.cn: 一般认为，这个词背后有一个表示「吃」的重构词根。

items.en: Fraetan means to eat up or devour.
items.cn: fraetan 意为吃光、吞食。

items.en: Fretan means to devour or gnaw, and also to wear something away.
items.cn: fretan 意为吞食、啃咬，也指把东西磨损掉。

items.en: Fret begins to mean to worry, as if worry were eating the mind.
items.cn: 中古英语中 fret 开始表示「忧虑」，仿佛忧虑在啃食心智。

items.en: Modern English keeps both the gnawing sense and the everyday worry sense.
items.cn: 现代英语同时保留「啃蚀」与日常「忧虑」两个义项。

note.en: Fret is the Germanic word for gnawing, and its family is all about small repeated vexation: fretful, fretfully, and the unrelated look-alike fretwork.
note.cn: fret 是日耳曼语中表示「啃咬」的词，它的词族都围绕反复的小烦恼：fretful、fretfully，以及只是拼写相近的 fretwork。

entries.definition: anxious and irritable
entries.definitionCN: 焦躁的；易怒的；由 fret 加 -ful 构成

entries.definition: in an anxious, irritable way
entries.definitionCN: 焦躁地；由 fretful 加 -ly 构成

entries.definition: carved ornamental work with interlacing lines
entries.definitionCN: 回纹雕饰；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to keep thinking about troubles
entries.definitionCN: 担心；发愁

entries.definition: to show unnecessary agitation about small things
entries.definitionCN: 为小事大惊小怪

entries.definition: to rub and become sore, or to become irritated
entries.definitionCN: 摩擦致痛；也指心里烦躁

normalIntro.en: Fret is gnawing: the same word once meant eating away, and worry does the same work on the mind.
normalIntro.cn: fret 是「啃咬」：这个词从前指把东西吃掉，而忧虑对心智做的正是同样的事。

normal.en: To fret about something is to keep chewing on it in your mind.
normal.cn: to fret about 某事，就是在心里反复咀嚼它。

normal.en: Fret over is the usual pairing, and in a fret means visibly anxious.
normal.cn: fret over 是最常见的搭配，in a fret 表示明显地焦躁不安。

normal.en: Fretful is the adjective, and fretfully the matching adverb.
normal.cn: fretful 是形容词，fretfully 是相配的副词。

normal.en: The old sense of eating away survives when acid frets metal.
normal.cn: 当酸液侵蚀金属时，那个古老的「啃蚀」义项仍然活着。

normal.en: Do not fret is the everyday comfort people offer.
normal.cn: Do not fret 是人们常说的安慰话。

abstract.en: Picture a finger tracing the same groove on a table for an hour.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指在桌面上同一道凹痕上来回划了一个小时。

abstract.en: Imagine a small stone in a shoe, nagging with every step.
abstract.cn: 想象鞋里有一颗小石子，每走一步都硌一下。

abstract.en: Think of a kettle that will not stop hissing after it leaves the stove.
abstract.cn: 想象一只水壶离开炉子后还在不停嘶响。

examples.en: She frets about money even when the bills are paid.
examples.cn: 即使账单都付清了，她还是为钱发愁。

examples.en: He fretted over the wording of the email all morning.
examples.cn: 他一整个上午都在为邮件的措辞纠结。

examples.en: The sea air frets the paint on the old gate.
examples.cn: 海风侵蚀着旧大门上的油漆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗瑞特」——像牙齿一点点啃咬，心里也一点点被磨；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 fretan（吞食、啃咬），源自原始日耳曼语 fraetan（吃光）→ 中古英语 fret（忧虑，如忧虑在啃食心智）→ 现代英语 fret，核心义「被一点点磨掉」。

sensesIntro.en: Fret begins with physical gnawing, turns into worry that gnaws at the mind, and then splits into a state noun and small repeated bouts.
sensesIntro.cn: fret 从物理上的「啃咬」开始，转为啃食心智的「忧虑」，再分出表状态的名词与一次次的小发作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand rubbing the same spot until the surface wears thin.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手反复摩挲同一处，直到表面被磨薄。

branches.en: Continuous worry is the mental form of gnawing.
branches.cn: 持续的忧虑是「啃咬」在心理层面的形态。

branches.en: Small details are the crumbs the mind keeps chewing.
branches.cn: 琐碎小事就是心智反复咀嚼的那些碎屑。

branches.en: What gnaws at one person can be felt as an irritation from outside.
branches.cn: 啃食一个人的东西，也可以被感受为来自外界的刺激。

branches.en: Corroding metal and chafing skin keep the oldest physical sense alive.
branches.cn: 侵蚀金属与磨痛皮肤让最古老的物理义项继续存活。

branches.en: The noun names both the state and the visible bout of restlessness.
branches.cn: 名词既指那种状态，也指看得见的一阵烦躁。

intro.en: Fret is a Germanic word with no Latin ancestor, and its English family grew around the idea of gnawing.
intro.cn: fret 是日耳曼语词，没有拉丁语祖先，它的英语词族围绕「啃咬」这一意念生长。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source here: fret goes back to Old English fretan and the Germanic root for eating.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语来源：fret 上溯到古英语 fretan 与表示「吃」的日耳曼语词根。

items.example: Fretan is the direct source of the modern verb.
items.exampleCN: fretan 是现代这个词的直接来源。

items.example: Fraetan is a reconstructed Germanic form.
items.exampleCN: fraetan 是重构出来的日耳曼语形式。

items.example: German fressen is a cousin of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 德语 fressen 是这个词的亲属词。

items.example: Fret keeps the worry sense of Middle English.
items.exampleCN: fret 保留了中古英语的「忧虑」义。

items.example: Fretted can describe both a person and a surface.
items.exampleCN: fretted 既可以形容人，也可以形容表面。

items.example: The suffix -ful forms fretful.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ful 构成 fretful。

items.example: Fretful describes a restless mood.
items.exampleCN: fretful 形容烦躁不安的情绪。

items.example: Fretfully modifies the way someone speaks.
items.exampleCN: fretfully 修饰人说话的方式。

items.example: Fretfulness names the mood itself.
items.exampleCN: fretfulness 指这种情绪本身。

definition_zh: 欢快的；兴高采烈的；满怀喜悦的；（有时）幸灾乐祸的
definition_en: feeling or showing a lively, open joy, and sometimes a secret pleasure at the misfortune of others
core_image: 一个人眼睛发亮、嘴角压不住地往上扬，快乐从全身透出来
scene: 雨后的院子里积着水洼，孩子们一脚踩进去，笑声追着水花跑。The children ran through the puddles with gleeful shouts.
sceneCN: 这里 gleeful 是「欢快的、兴高采烈的」（第 1 个义项：写在脸上、听得见的喜悦）；句意：孩子们一路欢叫着跑过水洼。

pos.zh: 形容词：欢快的；兴高采烈的；有时指幸灾乐祸的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「欢快地；兴高采烈地」
由本词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「欢快；兴高采烈」
本词的词根名词，义为「欢乐、欢庆」，也指多声部合唱歌曲

senses.title: Joy that shows on the face
senses.definition: showing bright, open happiness in the face, voice, or manner
senses.definitionCN: 在表情、声音或举止中流露出明朗、外显的快乐
senses.example: A gleeful smile spread across her face when she opened the parcel.
senses.exampleCN: 她打开包裹时，脸上绽开了欢快的笑容。
senses.why: Glee first named festivity and mirth, and the suffix -ful means full of, so a gleeful person is visibly full of that mirth.
senses.whyCN: glee 最初指欢庆与欢笑，后缀 -ful 意为「充满」；gleeful 的人就是明显写满了这份欢笑。

senses.title: A sudden rush of delight
senses.definition: feeling a strong, sudden delight about good news or a happy event
senses.definitionCN: 因好消息或喜事而突然感到强烈的喜悦
senses.example: She was gleeful when the letter finally arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 那封信终于寄到时，她满心欢喜。
senses.why: The adjective can describe the inner feeling as well as its outer sign: the mirth fills the mind before it reaches the face.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词既能写外在的迹象，也能写内心的感受：欢笑先充满心里，再流露到脸上。

senses.title: Childlike high spirits
senses.definition: noisily and playfully excited, in the way children often are
senses.definitionCN: 像孩子那样又吵又闹、带着玩心的兴奋
senses.example: The gleeful children chased each other around the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 欢闹的孩子们在花园里互相追逐。
senses.why: Glee also named play and sport, so its adjective keeps a hint of harmless, noisy game.
senses.whyCN: glee 也曾指游戏与嬉闹，所以它的形容词保留了无害而喧闹的玩闹意味。

senses.title: Pleasure at the misfortune of another
senses.definition: showing a secret or unkind satisfaction when something bad happens to another person
senses.definitionCN: 别人遭遇不顺时流露出的隐秘或不太厚道的满足
senses.example: His gleeful reaction when the rival team lost surprised everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 对手球队落败时他那副幸灾乐祸的样子，让所有人都很意外。
senses.why: Mirth can be turned toward the loss of another person; the same bright face then carries a darker edge.
senses.whyCN: 欢笑也可以指向别人的损失；同一张明亮的脸，此时就带上了一层暗色。

senses.title: Excited anticipation
senses.definition: excited and eager while waiting for something pleasant to happen
senses.definitionCN: 在等待好事发生时的兴奋与急切
senses.example: The fans were gleeful as the concert countdown began.
senses.exampleCN: 演唱会倒计时开始，歌迷们兴奋不已。
senses.why: Festive glee is often forward-looking: the celebration has not started, and the joy is already in the voice.
senses.whyCN: 节庆式的欢笑往往朝向未来：庆祝还没开始，喜悦已经先到了声音里。

senses.title: Triumphant satisfaction
senses.definition: openly pleased and satisfied after a win, a success, or an advantage
senses.definitionCN: 在获胜、成功或占到上风之后公开表露的满意与得意
senses.example: The team gave a gleeful wave to the crowd after the final whistle.
senses.exampleCN: 终场哨响后，球队朝观众席得意地挥手。
senses.why: A victory is a feast, and glee keeps the feast in it: the winner is filled with the joy of the celebration.
senses.whyCN: 胜利就是一场宴席，glee 保留了其中的宴饮意味：获胜者被庆祝的喜悦充满。

senses.title: Mirth in song and festivity
senses.titleCN: 歌唱与欢庆中的欢笑（旧义）
senses.definition: in older use, full of the merriment, music, and entertainment that glee once named
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的用法中，指充满 glee 旧义所指的欢笑、音乐与娱乐
senses.example: The gleeful company sang old songs late into the night.
senses.exampleCN: 欢腾的一群人唱着老歌，一直到深夜。
senses.why: This sense keeps the oldest layer of glee, which meant music and entertainment as much as laughter.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项保留着 glee 最古老的一层意思：它既指笑声，也指音乐与娱乐。

senses.title: Without restraint: gleeful abandon
senses.definition: in phrases such as gleeful abandon, joy that is let loose without self-control
senses.definitionCN: 用于 gleeful abandon 一类短语，指毫无克制地放开的欢乐
senses.example: The children slid down the hill with gleeful abandon.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们忘乎所以地从山坡上滑下来。
senses.why: When joy is full, restraint falls away; the adjective then describes not a mood but the way the whole body lets go.
senses.whyCN: 当喜悦满溢，克制就松开了；这时形容词写的不只是心情，而是整个身体放开的样子。

intro.en: Gleeful is an English compound of the old noun glee and the suffix -ful; the deeper origin of glee is not settled.
intro.cn: gleeful 是英语由古老名词 glee 加后缀 -ful 构成的复合词；glee 的更早来源尚无定论。

items.en: A Germanic ancestor is generally assumed behind Old English glēo, but no attested form survives, so any reconstruction is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为古英语 glēo 背后有一个日耳曼语来源，但没有留下可考的形式，因此任何重构都只能存疑。

items.en: Glēo meant mirth, music, entertainment, and mockery; it could name a feast and a jeer alike.
items.cn: glēo 意为欢笑、音乐、娱乐，也指嘲弄；它既能指宴饮欢庆，也能指讥笑。

items.en: The word narrowed toward mirth and merry company, and the spelling settled as glee.
items.cn: 这个词的意义收窄到欢笑与欢聚，拼写固定为 glee。

items.en: Glee plus -ful produced gleeful, first recorded in the later sixteenth century; the exact date is uncertain.
items.cn: glee 加 -ful 构成 gleeful，最早见于十六世纪后期；确切年代不确定。

items.en: Modern English extends the adjective from visible joy to eager anticipation and to pleasure taken in the loss of another.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个形容词从外显的欢乐扩展到急切期待，以及从别人的损失中取乐。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the glee family and one word that only shares the letters gle; the near-meaning group holds everyday joy adjectives of different strength.
note.cn: 形近组收 glee 词族，以及一个只是恰好共享开头几个字母的词；近义组收日常表示喜悦的形容词，强度各不相同。

entries.definition: The noun behind gleeful: mirth, merry entertainment, or a part-song for several voices.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，是 gleeful 的词根：欢笑、欢庆娱乐，也指多声部合唱歌曲。

entries.definition: The adverb formed from gleeful with -ly, meaning in a gleeful manner.
entries.definitionCN: 由 gleeful 加 -ly 构成的副词，义为「欢快地、兴高采烈地」。

entries.definition: To gather grain left in a field, or to collect information bit by bit; it only looks similar and comes from Old French.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「拾穗；一点点搜集信息」；只是拼写相近，词源不同，来自古法语。

entries.definition: Full of joy; warmer and more general than gleeful, with no hint of mockery.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「充满喜悦的」，比 gleeful 更温暖、更一般，不带嘲弄意味。

entries.definition: Bright and positive in mood; steadier and quieter than gleeful.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「开朗愉快的」，比 gleeful 更平稳、更安静。

entries.definition: Raised high by good news or success; more formal and more inward than gleeful.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「兴高采烈的」，多因好消息或成功而振奋，比 gleeful 更正式、更偏内心。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real glee family and the phrases the adjective actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 glee 词族，以及这个形容词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Glee is mirth, and -ful means full of, so gleeful is simply full of mirth.
normal.cn: glee 是欢笑，-ful 意为「充满」，所以 gleeful 就是「满是欢笑」。

normal.en: Glee also names a part-song, which is why a glee club sings rather than laughs.
normal.cn: glee 也指多声部合唱曲，所以 glee club 是唱合唱的团体，而不是大笑俱乐部。

normal.en: A gleeful smile and a gleeful shout both show joy that others can see and hear.
normal.cn: gleeful smile 与 gleeful shout 都表示别人看得见、听得见的喜悦。

normal.en: Gleeful can turn unkind: a gleeful reaction to a defeat is pleasure at the loss of someone else.
normal.cn: gleeful 也可能不厚道：对别人落败的 gleeful reaction 就是从他人的损失中取乐。

normal.en: Compare cheerful: cheerful is a steady warm mood, while gleeful is a livelier burst of mirth.
normal.cn: 对比 cheerful：cheerful 是平稳温暖的心情，gleeful 则是更活泼的一阵欢笑。

abstract.en: Picture a face lit from inside, the eyes bright and the mouth unable to stay level.
abstract.cn: 想象一张从里面被点亮的笑脸：眼睛发亮，嘴角怎么也压不平。

abstract.en: Think of a letter arriving with good news, and the small jump the body makes before the mind catches up.
abstract.cn: 想象一封带来好消息的信到手，身体先于头脑轻轻一跳。

abstract.en: See a pack of children running through puddles, shouting for the pure fun of shouting.
abstract.cn: 想象一群孩子跑过水洼，纯粹为了好玩而大声喊叫。

examples.en: A gleeful shout went up when the results were posted.
examples.cn: 成绩公布时，人群爆发出一阵欢呼。

examples.en: He was gleeful about the chance to try the new machine.
examples.cn: 他为有机会试用那台新机器而兴高采烈。

examples.en: The gleeful children would not sit still for the photograph.
examples.cn: 那些欢闹的孩子怎么也不肯坐着拍照。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「格里福」——格里一福，笑到出声：欢快、兴高采烈。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 glēo「欢笑、音乐、娱乐」+ 后缀 -ful「充满……的」→ gleeful「满怀欢笑的」；glēo 在古英语中可考，但其更早的日耳曼语来源属重构形式，确切来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses spread from visible joy to inner delight, childlike play, unkind pleasure, anticipation, triumph, festive song, and joy without restraint.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从外显的喜悦铺开：内心的欢喜、孩子气的玩闹、不厚道的取乐、期待、得意、节庆歌唱，以及毫无克制的欢乐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face lit from inside, eyes bright and mouth lifting.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张从里面被点亮的笑脸，眼睛发亮，嘴角上扬。

branches.en: THE FACE: joy becomes visible as a smile, a shout, a bright look.
branches.cn: 面部线：喜悦变成看得见的笑、喊声与明亮的目光。

branches.en: THE INNER FEELING: delight can fill the mind quietly or spill out as childish play.
branches.cn: 内心线：喜悦可以安静地充满心里，也可以化作孩子气的玩闹溢出来。

branches.en: THE DARK EDGE: the same mirth turns toward the loss of another person.
branches.cn: 暗色线：同一份欢笑转向别人的损失。

branches.en: THE FUTURE AND THE WIN: joy runs ahead to what is coming, and back to what has just been won.
branches.cn: 未来与胜利线：喜悦既跑向将要发生的事，也回到刚刚赢下的成果。

branches.en: THE OLD LAYER AND THE OPEN FLOOD: festive song is the oldest sense, and abandon is joy with no brake.
branches.cn: 旧义与放开线：节庆歌唱是最古老的一层，abandon 则是松开刹车的欢乐。

intro.en: Gleeful is an English noun plus an English suffix; the family is Germanic, not Latin, so no Latin cognates are listed.
intro.cn: gleeful 是英语名词加英语后缀构成；这个词族属日耳曼语层而非拉丁语层，因此不列拉丁同源词。

latinIntro.en: Glee has no recorded Latin ancestor and no Latin cognate; its documented history begins in Old English.
latinIntro.cn: glee 没有可考的拉丁语来源，也没有拉丁同源词；它可查的历史始于古英语。

items.example: Glēo is the documented starting point of the family.
items.exampleCN: glēo 是这一词族有文献记载的起点。

items.example: Glee keeps both the laughter and the song.
items.exampleCN: glee 同时保留了笑声与歌声。

items.example: The suffix turns glee into gleeful.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把 glee 变成 gleeful。

items.example: Gleeful is the adjective of the family.
items.exampleCN: gleeful 是这个词族的形容词。

items.example: It forms the adverb gleefully.
items.exampleCN: 它构成副词 gleefully。

items.example: Gleefully describes how someone laughs or shouts.
items.exampleCN: gleefully 描述人如何笑或如何喊。

items.example: It forms the noun gleefulness.
items.exampleCN: 它构成名词 gleefulness。

items.example: Gleefulness names the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: gleefulness 指这种性质本身。

items.example: A glee club sings part-songs.
items.exampleCN: glee club 演唱多声部合唱曲。

definition_zh: 滑行；滑翔；轻盈无声地移动；（时间）悄然流逝；滑音
definition_en: to move smoothly, quietly, and continuously with little effort or friction, or to pass in such a way
core_image: 一只鸟收拢翅膀，贴着水面无声地滑过去，几乎没有碰到任何东西
scene: 清晨的湖面结着一层薄冰，芦苇的影子一动不动。The heron glided low over the ice and landed without a sound.
sceneCN: 这里 glide 是「滑翔、滑行」（第 2 个义项：鸟类或飞行器不靠动力、平稳地掠过）；句意：苍鹭贴着薄冰低低滑过，无声落下。

pos.zh: 动词：滑行；滑翔；轻盈无声地移动；悄然流逝
名词：滑行；滑翔；语音学中的滑音

collocations.zh: 不知不觉地进入（某种状态）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加表示施动者的后缀 -er 构成，义为「滑翔机；滑翔者」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「滑翔；滑翔运动」
由 gliding 加 -ly 构成，义为「流畅地、滑行般地」，较少使用

senses.title: To move smoothly over a surface
senses.definition: to move smoothly and continuously along or over a surface, with little friction or effort
senses.definitionCN: 沿着或贴着某个表面平滑、连续地移动，几乎不费力
senses.example: The puck glided across the polished ice.
senses.exampleCN: 冰球在打磨过的冰面上滑了过去。
senses.why: The Old English verb meant to slip or slide along; the image is motion that meets almost no resistance.
senses.whyCN: 这个古英语动词意为「滑过、溜过」；意象是几乎遇不到阻力的运动。

senses.title: To fly without power
senses.definition: of a bird or aircraft, to fly smoothly downward or onward without using power
senses.definitionCN: 指鸟类或飞行器不使用动力，平稳地向下或向前飞行
senses.example: The gull glided down to the water without a single wingbeat.
senses.exampleCN: 海鸥一下翅膀也没扇，就滑翔到了水面。
senses.why: A glide is the purest kind of movement: gravity does the work and the wing only steers.
senses.whyCN: 滑翔是最纯粹的运动：重力做功，翅膀只负责掌方向。

senses.title: To move quietly and unnoticed
senses.definition: to move quietly and smoothly so that people hardly notice you
senses.definitionCN: 安静、平稳地移动，让人几乎察觉不到
senses.example: She glided through the crowded hall without disturbing anyone.
senses.exampleCN: 她悄无声息地穿过拥挤的大厅，没有打扰任何人。
senses.why: A smooth body leaves no noise and no jolt behind it, so the same verb serves for silent movement among people.
senses.whyCN: 平稳的身体不会留下声音和颠簸，所以同一个动词也能表示在人群中无声穿行。

senses.title: A smooth dancing or skating step
senses.definition: a smooth, flowing step or movement in dance, skating, or gymnastics
senses.definitionCN: 舞蹈、滑冰或体操中流畅、连贯的一步或一段移动
senses.example: The pair opened the waltz with a long glide across the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 两人以一段长长的滑步开始了这支华尔兹。
senses.why: Dance borrows the surface image directly: the foot travels without a bump, as if over ice.
senses.whyCN: 舞蹈直接借用了表面滑行的意象：脚移动时不带颠簸，仿佛在冰上。

senses.title: Of time: to pass quietly
senses.definition: of time, to pass smoothly and quickly, often without being noticed
senses.definitionCN: 指时间平稳而迅速地过去，往往不被察觉
senses.example: The long afternoon glided by in easy conversation.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的午后在轻松的交谈中悄悄过去了。
senses.why: Time is imagined as a surface, and its passing as a body moving over it without a sound.
senses.whyCN: 时间被想象成一个表面，它的流逝则像一个身体在上面无声地移动。

senses.title: A speech sound that slides
senses.titleCN: 滑音：音段之间的平滑过渡
senses.definition: in phonetics and music, a speech sound or tone that changes smoothly from one position to another
senses.definitionCN: 在语音学与音乐中，从一个位置平滑过渡到另一个位置的音
senses.example: The diphthong begins with a glide from a closed vowel.
senses.exampleCN: 这个双元音以一个从闭元音开始的滑音起头。
senses.why: The mouth changes shape gradually, so the sound glides instead of jumping.
senses.whyCN: 口腔逐渐改变形状，声音因此是滑过去的，而不是跳过去的。

senses.title: To change smoothly into a new state
senses.titleCN: 不知不觉地过渡到某种状态
senses.definition: to pass gradually and smoothly into a different state, role, or condition
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐、平稳地进入另一种状态、角色或处境
senses.example: The conversation glided into a friendly argument about music.
senses.exampleCN: 谈话不知不觉变成了一场关于音乐的友好争论。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the no-jolt image and applies it to change itself: no sharp border, only a slope.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了「没有颠簸」的意象，并把它用到变化本身：没有突兀的边界，只有一段缓坡。

senses.title: To pass over something lightly
senses.definition: in phrases such as glide over, to avoid dealing with a problem or to mention it only briefly
senses.definitionCN: 用于 glide over 一类短语，指避开处理某个问题，或只是轻轻提一下
senses.example: The report glided over the cost of the project.
senses.exampleCN: 报告对项目的成本只是轻描淡写地带过。
senses.why: If a body glides over a surface, it never presses down on it; skipping a problem is the same light touch.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个物体从表面上滑过，它就从未真正压下去；略过问题也是同样的轻触。

intro.en: Glide is a native Germanic verb recorded in Old English, and it stays close to its original image of smooth, low-friction motion.
intro.cn: glide 是记录于古英语的本族日耳曼语动词，至今仍贴近它最初那个平滑、低摩擦运动的意象。

items.en: A verb *glīdaną is reconstructed for Proto-Germanic; because it is a reconstruction, its exact shape is not certain.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语中重构出一个动词 *glīdaną；由于是重构形式，其确切形态并不确定。

items.en: Glīdan meant to glide, slip, or slide, and it described both bodies and things moving smoothly.
items.cn: glīdan 意为滑过、溜过、滑动，既能写人也能写物，都指平滑地移动。

items.en: The verb survives as gliden with the same smooth-motion sense; the modern spelling glide follows later.
items.cn: 这个动词以 gliden 的形式留存，仍指平滑运动；现代拼写 glide 出现得更晚。

items.en: The noun glide appears later, and in the nineteenth century glider comes to name an engine-less flying machine.
items.cn: 名词 glide 出现较晚；十九世纪 glider 开始指没有发动机的飞行器。

items.en: Aviation, phonetics, dance, and figurative transitions all extend the same image of motion without a jolt.
items.cn: 航空、语音学、舞蹈与比喻性的过渡，都延伸着同一个「没有颠簸」的运动意象。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the gliding family and a word from a related Germanic root; the near-meaning group gathers other smooth-motion verbs.
note.cn: 形近组收滑行词族，以及一个来自相关日耳曼词根的词；近义组收其它表示平滑运动的动词。

entries.definition: An aircraft that flies without an engine, or a person or thing that glides.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「滑翔机」，也指滑翔的人或物。

entries.definition: The sport of flying a glider, or the present participle of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「滑翔运动」，也是动词的现在分词。

entries.definition: To move over a surface while staying in contact with it; it belongs to a related Germanic family and is not formed from glide.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「在表面上滑动、打滑」；与 glide 同属一个日耳曼词族，但不是由它派生，另有独立来源。

entries.definition: To slide a short way, often by accident or with a loss of grip.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「滑一下、失足」，多指意外或失去抓力。

entries.definition: To be carried slowly by a current of air or water; passive rather than controlled.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「漂流、飘移」，是被气流或水流带着走，而非自己掌控。

entries.definition: To stay on or near the surface of a liquid, or to move lightly in the air.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「漂浮、飘浮」，指停留在液体表面或在空中轻飘。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Germanic root and the phrases glide actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的日耳曼词根，以及 glide 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Old English glīdan means to slip along, and the modern verb has never lost that smoothness.
normal.cn: 古英语 glīdan 意为「滑过去」，现代动词一直没丢掉这份平滑。

normal.en: A glider is the thing that glides: the suffix -er simply marks the doer or the machine.
normal.cn: glider 就是会滑翔的东西：后缀 -er 只标记动作的发出者或机器。

normal.en: To glide over a problem is to pass it without pressing down on it.
normal.cn: glide over a problem 就是从问题上滑过去，不真正压下去。

normal.en: To glide into a new state means to enter it so gradually that no border is felt.
normal.cn: glide into a new state 意为进入新状态时缓得让人感觉不到边界。

normal.en: Compare slide: slide keeps contact and friction, while glide suggests almost none.
normal.cn: 对比 slide：slide 保有接触与摩擦，glide 则暗示几乎没有摩擦。

abstract.en: See a heron folding its wings and coasting one hand width above the water.
abstract.cn: 想象一只苍鹭收拢翅膀，在水面上方一掌宽的高度滑行。

abstract.en: Think of a flat stone skimming a pond: no engine, no beat, only a long shallow curve.
abstract.cn: 想象一块扁石在水面上打水漂：没有引擎，没有拍击，只有一道又长又浅的弧。

abstract.en: Picture a person crossing a crowded room so smoothly that nobody turns around.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人穿过满屋的人，平稳得没有一个人回头。

examples.en: The dancer glided across the stage as if the floor were ice.
examples.cn: 舞者滑过舞台，仿佛地板是冰面。

examples.en: Time glides by when the work is interesting.
examples.cn: 做有意思的工作时，时间过得飞快。

examples.en: The plane glided for two kilometres after the engine failed.
examples.cn: 引擎失效后，飞机滑翔了两公里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「格莱德」——格拉一滑，贴地无声：滑行、滑翔。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 glīdan「滑过、溜过」，与 slīdan（slide）同属一个日耳曼语「滑动」词族；原始日耳曼语 *glīdaną 属重构形式，更早的印欧词根不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one smooth motion: over a surface, through the air, past people, in dance, through time, in speech, into a new state, and over a problem.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一种平滑运动展开：贴着表面、穿过空气、经过人群、在舞蹈里、随时间、在语音中、进入新状态，以及掠过问题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heron with folded wings coasting one hand width above still water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只收拢翅膀的苍鹭，在水面上方一掌宽处滑过。

branches.en: THE SURFACE: a body travels over ice, a floor, or a rink without a bump.
branches.cn: 表面线：身体在冰面、地板或冰场上平稳移动，没有颠簸。

branches.en: THE AIR: gravity and wing shape replace the engine.
branches.cn: 空中线：重力和翼形取代了发动机。

branches.en: THE CROWD: the same quiet motion passes through people unnoticed.
branches.cn: 人群线：同样的安静运动从人群中穿过而不被察觉。

branches.en: TIME: passing time is imagined as a body moving over a surface.
branches.cn: 时间线：时间的流逝被想象成物体在表面上移动。

branches.en: THE ABSTRACT: sound, states, and problems all get the same light, borderless touch.
branches.cn: 抽象线：声音、状态与问题都得到同样轻盈、无边界的一触。

intro.en: Glide is a native Germanic verb; its family is built with English suffixes and compounds, not with Latin affixes.
intro.cn: glide 是日耳曼语本族动词；它的词族由英语后缀与复合词构成，与拉丁语词缀无关。

latinIntro.en: Glide has no Latin ancestor and no Latin cognate, so the Latin list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: glide 没有拉丁语来源，也没有拉丁同源词，因此拉丁同源词一栏留空。

items.example: The reconstructed verb is the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个重构动词是这一词族的基础。

items.example: Glīdan is the first recorded form.
items.exampleCN: glīdan 是最早有记录的形式。

items.example: Gliden carries the verb into Middle English.
items.exampleCN: gliden 把这个动词带入中古英语。

items.example: Glide keeps the old motion image.
items.exampleCN: glide 保留了古老的运动意象。

items.example: It forms glider.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 glider。

items.example: A glider rides on gravity and air.
items.exampleCN: 滑翔机靠重力和空气飞行。

items.example: It forms gliding.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 gliding。

items.meaning: the sport of flying a glider
items.example: Gliding is the sport built on the verb.
items.exampleCN: gliding 是由这个动词发展出的运动。

items.meaning: the approach path of an aircraft
items.example: The glide path guides a landing aircraft.
items.exampleCN: glide path 引导飞机降落。

items.example: Glidingly is a rare adverb of manner.
items.exampleCN: glidingly 是较少用的方式副词。

definition_zh: 阴暗的；阴沉的；忧郁的；悲观的；萧条的
definition_en: dark or dim in a depressing way, or sad, hopeless, and without cheer
core_image: 一间没有开灯的房间，灰白的光只从窄缝里漏进来，空气湿冷
scene: 停电之后的走廊只剩一扇小窗，透进灰白的光，墙角的灰泥冒着潮气。The gloomy corridor smelled of damp plaster and old dust.
sceneCN: 这里 gloomy 是「昏暗的、阴暗的」（第 1 个义项：光线不足而显得压抑的空间）；句意：昏暗的走廊里有湿灰泥和旧尘土的气味。

pos.zh: 形容词：阴暗的；阴沉的；忧郁的；悲观的；萧条的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「阴郁地；昏暗地」
由本词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「阴暗；忧郁」
本词的词根名词，义为「昏暗；忧郁」

senses.title: A place with too little light
senses.definition: dimly lit and depressing to be in
senses.definitionCN: 光线昏暗，让人待着觉得压抑
senses.example: The cellar was gloomy even at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 那个地窖即使正午也昏暗阴沉。
senses.why: Gloom first named dark weather and a darkened look; a room without light is the image at its plainest.
senses.whyCN: gloom 最初指昏暗的天气与阴沉的脸色；没有光的房间是这一意象最朴素的形态。

senses.title: Sad and without cheer
senses.definition: sad, quiet, and lacking any cheer in mood or expression
senses.definitionCN: 情绪或表情上悲伤、沉默，毫无喜色
senses.example: He sat gloomy and silent through the whole evening.
senses.exampleCN: 他整个晚上都坐在那里，阴郁而沉默。
senses.why: Darkness outside was early read as darkness inside; a gloomy person carries the unlit room in the face.
senses.whyCN: 外面的昏暗很早就被读成心里的昏暗；忧郁的人把没开灯的房间带在了脸上。

senses.title: Expecting the worst
senses.definition: pessimistic about the future, expecting things to go badly
senses.definitionCN: 对未来持悲观态度，预期事情会变糟
senses.example: The forecast for the industry is gloomy.
senses.exampleCN: 这个行业的前景预测十分悲观。
senses.why: If the light is failing, the road ahead cannot be seen; pessimism is that image moved from eyesight to expectation.
senses.whyCN: 如果光线在暗下去，前方的路就看不见；悲观主义就是把这一意象从视觉移到了预期。

senses.title: Dreary and oppressive in atmosphere
senses.definition: of an event, gathering, or period, dull and heavy in mood
senses.definitionCN: 指活动、聚会或时期的气氛沉闷、沉重
senses.example: The meeting ended in a gloomy silence.
senses.exampleCN: 会议在一种沉闷的沉默中结束。
senses.why: A dark room presses on the people in it; an occasion can carry the same weight without any walls.
senses.whyCN: 昏暗的房间会压迫里面的人；一场活动即使没有墙壁，也能带上同样的重量。

senses.title: Economically depressed
senses.definition: of trade, industry, or a market, weak and discouraging
senses.definitionCN: 指贸易、工业或市场疲弱、令人沮丧
senses.example: Factory orders have been gloomy for three quarters.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂订单已经连续三个季度不景气。
senses.why: The image of failing light serves an economy that seems to be dimming, with no clear dawn ahead.
senses.whyCN: 光线变暗的意象正好用于仿佛正在变暗、看不到明确黎明的经济。

senses.title: Dark and sinister, in story and scene
senses.titleCN: 阴森可怖的（文学与场景描写）
senses.definition: in literary description, dark in a way that suggests danger, death, or evil
senses.definitionCN: 在文学描写中，指暗得暗示危险、死亡或邪恶
senses.example: A gloomy castle stood above the village in every ghost story.
senses.exampleCN: 每个鬼故事里都有一座阴森的城堡立在村子上方。
senses.why: Darkness hides what is there, and what is hidden can be feared; literature turns the dim room into an omen.
senses.whyCN: 黑暗藏起了那里的东西，而被藏起的东西令人恐惧；文学把昏暗的房间变成了预兆。

senses.title: Dull and dark in colour
senses.definition: of a colour, dark and muted, with no brightness or life
senses.definitionCN: 指颜色深、暗、含灰，没有明亮与生气
senses.example: The walls were painted a gloomy grey-brown.
senses.exampleCN: 墙壁被刷成一种沉闷的灰褐色。
senses.why: Colour is light reflected; a colour without light is the gloom of the room fixed on a surface.
senses.whyCN: 颜色是被反射的光；缺少光的颜色，就是房间的昏暗被固定在了某个表面上。

senses.title: Overcast and threatening, of weather
senses.definition: of weather, heavily overcast, dull, and likely to rain
senses.definitionCN: 指天气乌云密布、灰暗，像要下雨
senses.example: A gloomy sky hung over the harbour all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 整个上午，阴霾的天空都压在港口上方。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer of all: gloom began as a word for dark, heavy weather.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：gloom 最初就是用来形容昏暗、沉重的天气。

intro.en: Gloomy is the adjective of gloom, a Middle English word whose own origin is not settled; the family is not recorded in Old English.
intro.cn: gloomy 是 gloom 的形容词，而 gloom 是中古英语词，其来源本身尚无定论；这个词族在古英语中未见记录。

items.en: Gloom is not recorded in Old English. Its origin is uncertain, and a Scandinavian source is often suggested but not proven.
items.cn: gloom 在古英语中未见记录。其来源不确定，常有人提出借自斯堪的纳维亚语，但未获证实。

items.en: Middle English gloum and glomen meant a sullen look and dark, heavy weather.
items.cn: 中古英语 gloum 与 glomen 指阴沉的脸色和昏暗沉重的天气。

items.en: The noun gloom and the adjective gloomy, formed with -y, appear in the sixteenth century; exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 名词 gloom 与加 -y 构成的形容词 gloomy 见于十六世纪；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The word widens: industry and trade are called gloomy, and gothic fiction uses it for ominous darkness.
items.cn: 词义扩大：工业与贸易被称作 gloomy，哥特小说则用它写不祥的黑暗。

items.en: Modern English applies it freely to mood, weather, colour, rooms, and economic outlook.
items.cn: 现代英语把它自由地用于心情、天气、颜色、房间与经济前景。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the gloom family and one word with another root that merely looks close; the near-meaning group holds dark and dreary adjectives of different reach.
note.cn: 形近组收 gloom 词族，以及一个只是拼写相近、词源不同的词；近义组收表示黑暗与凄凉的形容词，范围各不相同。

entries.definition: The noun behind gloomy: partial darkness, and a mood of sadness or low spirits.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，是 gloomy 的词根：半明半暗，也指悲伤低落的情绪。

entries.definition: The adverb formed with -ly, meaning in a gloomy manner.
entries.definitionCN: 由 gloomy 加 -ly 构成的副词，义为「阴郁地；昏暗地」。

entries.definition: Twilight, or the dim light of evening; it looks close to gloom but comes from a different Old English word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「黄昏、暮色」；拼写与 gloom 相近，但来自另一个古英语词，词源不同。

entries.definition: With little or no light; it states the fact of light and carries less emotion than gloomy.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「黑暗的」，只陈述光线状况，比 gloomy 少一些情绪。

entries.definition: Cheerless and dreary, often of weather, places, or prospects.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「凄凉阴沉的」，多用于天气、地方或前景，比 gloomy 更强调凄惨。

entries.definition: Dull, monotonous, and tiring; it stresses boredom rather than darkness.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「单调乏味的、令人厌倦的」，强调乏味而非黑暗。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Middle English root and the phrases gloomy appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的中古英语词源，以及 gloomy 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Gloom is not an Old English word: the family begins in Middle English with a sullen look and dark weather.
normal.cn: gloom 不是古英语词：这一词族始于中古英语，指阴沉的脸色和昏暗的天气。

normal.en: The suffix -y turns the noun gloom into the adjective gloomy, just as it turns rain into rainy.
normal.cn: 后缀 -y 把名词 gloom 变成形容词 gloomy，就像把 rain 变成 rainy 一样。

normal.en: A gloomy face and gloomy weather both lack light, one inside and one outside.
normal.cn: gloomy face 与 gloomy weather 都缺少光，一个在里，一个在外。

normal.en: Gloomy about the future is the same dark room moved into expectation.
normal.cn: gloomy about the future 就是把同一间暗屋子搬进了对未来的预期里。

normal.en: Compare dismal and dreary: dismal adds misery, dreary adds boredom, gloomy keeps the image of failing light.
normal.cn: 对比 dismal 与 dreary：dismal 多了凄惨，dreary 多了乏味，gloomy 则保留光线变暗的意象。

abstract.en: Picture a corridor where one small window lets in grey light and the air smells of wet plaster.
abstract.cn: 想象一条走廊，只有一扇小窗透进灰白的光，空气里有湿灰泥的味道。

abstract.en: Think of a face that has forgotten how to lift at the corners.
abstract.cn: 想象一张忘了怎么把嘴角抬起来的脸。

abstract.en: See a weather chart covered by one flat grey cloud, with no break in it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张天气图被一整片平坦的灰云盖住，中间没有一道缝隙。

examples.en: The basement flat was cold and gloomy in winter.
examples.cn: 那间地下公寓冬天又冷又阴暗。

examples.en: She felt gloomy about the move to a new city.
examples.cn: 她对搬去一座新城市感到忧郁。

examples.en: Economists gave a gloomy forecast for next year.
examples.cn: 经济学家对明年的预测并不乐观。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「格鲁米」——格鲁一沉，屋里没灯：阴暗、忧郁。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 中古英语 gloum「脸色阴沉、天色昏暗」，古英语未见记录；一般认为可能借自斯堪的纳维亚语，确切来源不确定。加后缀 -y 构成 gloomy「阴沉的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses darken one image: an unlit room, a sad face, a bad forecast, a heavy occasion, a weak economy, a sinister castle, a dull colour, and an overcast sky.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一个意象压暗：没开灯的房间、忧郁的脸、糟糕的预测、沉重的场合、疲弱的经济、阴森的城堡、沉闷的颜色，以及阴霾的天空。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an unlit room where grey light enters through one narrow gap.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间没开灯的房间，灰白的光只从一道窄缝里进来。

branches.en: THE ROOM: too little light makes a place oppressive.
branches.cn: 房间线：光线太少让空间变得压抑。

branches.en: THE MOOD: the unlit room is carried into a face and into a gathering.
branches.cn: 情绪线：没开灯的房间被带到了脸上，也带进了一场聚会。

branches.en: THE FORECAST: failing light becomes a poor outlook, for a career or for an economy.
branches.cn: 预测线：光线变暗变成了对职业或经济的不良预期。

branches.en: THE SURFACE: literature turns darkness into an omen, and a colour keeps the dimness.
branches.cn: 表面线：文学把黑暗变成预兆，颜色则把昏暗保留下来。

branches.en: THE SKY: the oldest layer, where gloom named heavy, dark weather.
branches.cn: 天空线：最古老的一层，gloom 曾专指昏暗沉重的天气。

intro.en: Gloomy is an English noun with an English suffix; the documented family starts in Middle English, and no Latin cognate exists.
intro.cn: gloomy 是英语名词加英语后缀构成；可考的这个词族始于中古英语，没有拉丁同源词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor and no Latin cognate for gloom, so the Latin list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: gloom 没有拉丁语来源，也没有拉丁同源词，因此拉丁同源词一栏留空。

items.meaningCN: 阴沉的脸色；昏暗的天气
items.example: Gloum is the earliest recorded form of the family.
items.exampleCN: gloum 是这一词族最早有记录的形式。

items.example: The verb described a face or a sky turning dark.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词描述脸或天空转暗。

items.example: Gloom keeps both the outer and the inner darkness.
items.exampleCN: gloom 同时保留外在的昏暗与内心的阴郁。

items.example: It forms gloomy from gloom.
items.exampleCN: 它把 gloom 变成 gloomy。

items.example: Gloomy is the adjective of the family.
items.exampleCN: gloomy 是这个词族的形容词。

items.example: It forms the adverb gloomily.
items.exampleCN: 它构成副词 gloomily。

items.example: Gloomily describes how someone speaks or looks.
items.exampleCN: gloomily 描述人说话或看人的样子。

items.example: It forms the noun gloominess.
items.exampleCN: 它构成名词 gloominess。

items.example: Gloominess names the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: gloominess 指这种性质本身。

definition_zh: 光泽；光亮；注释；释义；简释
definition_en: a shine on a surface, or a short note that explains a word
core_image: 一层薄亮的漆覆在表面，光顺着它滑过去
scene: 新刷的桌面还没干透，灯一照就泛出一层亮。The fresh varnish gave the table a deep gloss.
sceneCN: 这里 gloss 是「光泽；光亮表面」（第 1 个义项：物体表面反光形成的一层亮泽）；句意是新刷的清漆让桌面泛出深沉的光泽。

pos.zh: 光泽；光亮表面；注释；释义
使有光泽；给……上光；注释；掩饰

derivatives.zh: 由 gloss 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「有光泽的；光面的」
由 glossy 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「光泽度」
由 glossy 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「光亮地」
由 gloss 加表示汇集的后缀 -ary 构成，义为「术语表」

senses.title: A shine on a surface
senses.definition: a smooth shine that light makes on the surface of something
senses.definitionCN: 光线在物体表面形成的平滑亮泽
senses.example: The polished wood had a warm gloss.
senses.exampleCN: 打磨过的木头泛着温暖的光泽。
senses.why: The shine word is probably northern, and it names the light that seems to lie on top of a surface.
senses.whyCN: 表示「光亮」的这个词很可能来自北方语言，它指那层仿佛铺在表面上的光。

senses.title: A short explanatory note
senses.definition: a brief note that explains the meaning of a word or phrase in a text
senses.definitionCN: 对文中词语或短语的含义所作的简短说明
senses.example: The editor added a gloss beside each archaic word.
senses.exampleCN: 编者为每个古旧词在旁加了注释。
senses.why: This sense comes from Greek glōssa, a word that itself needed explaining, and Latin glossa, an explanatory note.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自希腊语 glōssa（本身需要解释的词）与拉丁语 glossa（解释性注释），所以「注释」是它的老本行。

senses.title: To give a surface a shine
senses.definition: to put a shine on a surface, or to make something look smooth and bright
senses.definitionCN: 给表面增加亮泽，或使某物显得光滑明亮
senses.example: She glossed the clay pot before it dried.
senses.exampleCN: 她在陶罐干透前给它上了光。
senses.why: The verb simply turns the shine noun into an action: putting the bright layer on.
senses.whyCN: 动词只是把「光泽」这个名词变成动作：把那层亮光加上去。

senses.title: To explain a word briefly
senses.definition: to add a short explanation to a word or phrase, especially in a text
senses.definitionCN: 在文本中为词语或短语添加简短解释
senses.example: The teacher glossed the difficult line in the margin.
senses.exampleCN: 老师在页边为那句难懂的话作了注解。
senses.why: The note sense became a verb: writing a gloss is to gloss a passage.
senses.whyCN: 「注释」这一名词义发展成动词：写一条注释就是给一段文字作注。

senses.title: To cover up a problem
senses.definition: to treat a problem or fault as if it were small or not worth attention
senses.definitionCN: 把问题或过失说得很小，仿佛不值得注意
senses.example: The report glossed over the loss of several jobs.
senses.exampleCN: 报告轻描淡写地带过了几个岗位的流失。
senses.why: A gloss is a smooth surface, and glossing over puts a smooth layer over a rough fact.
senses.whyCN: gloss 本是光滑的表面，而 gloss over 就是给粗糙的事实盖上一层光滑的膜，所以引申为掩饰。

intro.en: Gloss is two words in one spelling: a note word from Greek glōssa through Latin, and a shine word of uncertain northern origin.
intro.cn: gloss 是拼写相同的两个词：一个来自希腊语 glōssa、经拉丁语而来的「注释」词，另一个是来源不确定的北方「光亮」词。

items.en: Glōssa meant the tongue, then language, and also a word that needed explaining.
items.cn: 希腊语 glōssa 本指舌头，又指语言，也指需要解释的难词。

items.en: Glossa took the sense of an explanatory note on an obscure word.
items.cn: 拉丁语 glossa 取得「对难解词语的注释」这一含义。

items.en: Glose named such a note, and gloser meant to write one.
items.cn: 古法语 glose 指这类注释，动词 gloser 意为写注。

items.en: Gloss entered English as a marginal note, often on a difficult text.
items.cn: gloss 以页边注释的身份进入英语，常用于难解的文本。

items.en: The shine sense appears in the sixteenth century, probably from Scandinavian or Low German.
items.cn: 表示光亮的义项在十六世纪出现，可能来自斯堪的纳维亚语或低地德语。

items.en: The two senses now share one spelling, and gloss over adds the idea of covering.
items.cn: 两个义项如今共用一种拼写，而 gloss over 又增添了「覆盖」的意思。

note.en: The first group gathers the gloss word family; the second gathers words for shine and for notes.
note.cn: 第一组收 gloss 的词族，第二组收表示光泽与注释的词。

entries.definition: a list of terms with their meanings
entries.definitionCN: 术语表（由 gloss 加 -ary 构成）

entries.definition: shiny and smooth
entries.definitionCN: 有光泽的（由 gloss 加 -y 构成）

entries.definition: to explain or comment, now archaic
entries.definitionCN: 注释；解说（古旧词，与 gloss 同源）

entries.definition: a soft, gentle shine
entries.definitionCN: 柔和的光泽

entries.definition: a bright reflected light, especially on metal
entries.definitionCN: 光彩；金属表面的亮光

entries.definition: a note added to explain part of a text
entries.definitionCN: 注解；注释

normalIntro.en: Gloss is a double word: a note in the margin and a shine on a surface share one spelling.
normalIntro.cn: gloss 是个双面词：页边的注释与表面的亮光共用一种拼写。

normal.en: The note gloss comes from Greek glōssa, a word that needed explaining.
normal.cn: 注释义的 gloss 来自希腊语 glōssa，本指需要解释的词。

normal.en: A gloss sits in the margin and explains one hard word.
normal.cn: 一条 gloss 待在页边，解释一个难词。

normal.en: Gloss over means to lay a smooth coat over a fault.
normal.cn: gloss over 意为给过失盖上一层光滑的外衣。

normal.en: Glossary collects glosses, glossy adds shine, and gloze is the old verb for explaining.
normal.cn: glossary 汇集注释，glossy 添上光泽，gloze 是表示解释的古旧动词。

normal.en: Lip gloss and gloss paint both name a thin shiny layer.
normal.cn: lip gloss 与 gloss paint 都指薄薄的一层亮光。

abstract.en: See a thin coat of varnish catching the lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一层薄清漆接住灯光。

abstract.en: See a small pencil note beside an old word.
abstract.cn: 想象一个古旧词旁边的小铅笔注。

abstract.en: See a hand brushing a shine onto a clay pot.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把光刷到陶罐上。

examples.en: The new paint has a soft gloss in the sunlight.
examples.cn: 新漆在阳光下泛着柔和的光泽。

examples.en: A gloss in the margin explains the strange phrase.
examples.cn: 页边的一条注释解释了那个奇怪的短语。

examples.en: The summary glosses over the real cost of the plan.
examples.cn: 摘要轻描淡写地带过了这项计划的真实成本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「光溜丝」——表面光溜得像丝线；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 注释义的 gloss 来自希腊语 glōssa（舌头、语言、难解之词），经拉丁语 glossa（注释）与古法语 glose 进入英语；光亮义的 gloss 来源不确定，一般认为来自斯堪的纳维亚语或低地德语，十六世纪才出现。两词同形却不同源。

sensesIntro.en: Gloss begins with the light on a surface, then moves to the written note, and finally to the acts of polishing, explaining and covering up.
sensesIntro.cn: gloss 从表面上的亮光出发，转到写在页边的注释，最后发展出上光、解释与掩饰等动作义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin bright layer on a surface, and a small note beside a hard word.
core.cn: 核心意象：表面上一层薄薄的亮光，以及难词旁边的一小条注释。

branches.en: The shine sense names the light lying on a surface.
branches.cn: 光泽义指铺在表面上的那层光。

branches.en: The note sense explains one hard word in a text.
branches.cn: 注释义解释文本中一个难懂的词。

branches.en: The verbs put a shine on an object or a note beside a word.
branches.cn: 动词义既指给物体上光，也指在词旁作注。

branches.en: Glossing over hides a fault under a smooth surface.
branches.cn: gloss over 把过失藏在光滑的表面之下。

branches.en: A smooth shine and a cover-up both work by what shows on top.
branches.cn: 光滑的亮泽与掩饰都靠表面呈现来起作用。

intro.en: Gloss carries two families: notes from Greek glōssa through Latin, and shine from an uncertain northern source.
intro.cn: gloss 带着两个词族：一个是从希腊语 glōssa 经拉丁语而来的注释词族，另一个是来源不明的北方光亮词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin glossa means an explanatory note and comes from Greek glōssa, the tongue or a hard word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 glossa 意为解释性注释，源自希腊语 glōssa（舌头或难解之词）。

items.example: Glōssa also named a word that needed explaining.
items.exampleCN: glōssa 也指需要解释的词。

items.example: Latin glossa is the direct source of the note sense.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 glossa 是注释义的直接来源。

items.example: Glossarium grew into English glossary.
items.exampleCN: glossarium 后来演变为英语 glossary。

items.example: Gloss carries both senses today.
items.exampleCN: gloss 今天兼有这两个义项。

items.example: Gloze is the old cousin of gloss.
items.exampleCN: gloze 是 gloss 的古旧同族词。

items.example: The suffix -y forms glossy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成 glossy。

items.example: The suffix -ary forms glossary.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ary 构成 glossary。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms glossiness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 glossiness。

items.meaning: to cover up or treat lightly
items.example: Gloss over hides a fault under a smooth word.
items.exampleCN: gloss over 用顺滑的措辞掩盖过失。

definition_zh: 术语表；词汇表；注释集；难词表
definition_en: a list of special terms with their meanings, usually placed at the end of a book
core_image: 书末几页按字母排好的术语，每条后面跟着一句解释
scene: 读到最后一章，学生翻到书后那张按字母排好的表。The glossary at the back explains every technical term in the chapter.
sceneCN: 这里 glossary 是「书末术语表」（第 1 个义项：附在书后、按字母排列并解释专门词语的表）；句意是书后的术语表解释了本章的每个专业词。

pos.zh: 术语表；词汇表；注释集

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语 glōssa 经拉丁语而来的基础词，义为「注释；光泽」
由 glossary 加形容词后缀 -ial 构成，义为「术语表的；注释的」
由 glossary 加表示人的后缀 -ist 构成，义为「编写注释或术语表的人」

senses.title: A term list at the end of a book
senses.definition: a list of terms with short definitions, printed at the end of a book
senses.definitionCN: 附在书末、收录专门词语并给出简短释义的表
senses.example: The glossary at the back defines each key term.
senses.exampleCN: 书后的术语表为每个关键术语下了定义。
senses.why: Glossarium was a collection of glosses, and a book placed that collection at its end.
senses.whyCN: glossarium 本是注释的汇集，书本把这份汇集放在末尾，于是有了书末术语表。

senses.title: A reference work for a subject
senses.titleCN: 专业词汇表；学科术语词典
senses.definition: a stand-alone reference work that explains the vocabulary of a subject
senses.definitionCN: 独立成书、解释某一学科词语的参考工具
senses.example: She published a glossary of medical vocabulary.
senses.exampleCN: 她出版了一部医学词汇术语表。
senses.why: Any field can gather its own terms into a glossarium, so the list grew into a subject dictionary.
senses.whyCN: 任何领域都能把自己的术语汇成 glossarium，于是这份清单长成了一部学科词典。

senses.title: A collection of explanatory notes
senses.definition: a collection of explanatory notes on a difficult text, especially an old one
senses.definitionCN: 对难解文本尤其是古旧文本所作的注释汇编
senses.example: Scholars compiled a glossary for the old poem.
senses.exampleCN: 学者们为这首古诗编了一部注释集。
senses.why: The first glossaries were notes on hard words in manuscripts, not lists at the back.
senses.whyCN: 最早的 glossary 是对手稿中难词的注释，而不是书末的词表。

senses.title: A word list for learners
senses.definition: a short list of hard words with meanings, prepared for learners of a text
senses.definitionCN: 为学习某篇文本的人准备的难词简表
senses.example: The school reader includes a glossary beside the text.
senses.exampleCN: 这本学校读本在正文旁附了一份难词表。
senses.why: A teacher who explains hard words one by one is making a small glossary for learners.
senses.whyCN: 老师把难词逐个解释，就是在为学习者编一份小型 glossary。

intro.en: Glossary comes from Latin glossarium, a collection of glosses, which goes back to Greek glōssa, a tongue or a hard word.
intro.cn: glossary 来自拉丁语 glossarium（注释的汇集），更远处可上溯到希腊语 glōssa（舌头或难解之词）。

items.en: Glōssa meant the tongue, then language, and also an obscure word that needed explaining.
items.cn: 希腊语 glōssa 指舌头，又指语言，也指需要解释的生僻词。

items.en: Glossa named the explanatory note written for such a word.
items.cn: 拉丁语 glossa 指为这类词写下的解释性注释。

items.en: Glossarium meant a collection of glosses, a word list with explanations.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 glossarium 意为注释的汇集，即带解释的词表。

items.en: English took glossary in the late fourteenth century for a collection of notes.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪晚期吸收 glossary，指注释的汇编。

items.en: Printed books put the glossary at the end and arranged it alphabetically.
items.cn: 印刷书籍把术语表放在书末，并按字母顺序编排。

items.en: Today the word covers subject dictionaries and online term lists.
items.cn: 如今这个词也涵盖学科词典与在线术语表。

note.en: The first group gathers the gloss family; the second gathers other names for word lists and reference works.
note.cn: 第一组收 gloss 词族，第二组收其他表示词表与工具书的词。

entries.definition: a short explanatory note
entries.definitionCN: 注释（glossary 的基础词）

entries.definition: relating to a glossary
entries.definitionCN: 术语表的；注释的（由 glossary 加 -ial 构成）

entries.definition: a writer of glosses or a glossary
entries.definitionCN: 注释编写者；术语表编者（由 glossary 加 -ist 构成）

entries.definition: the vocabulary of a language or subject
entries.definitionCN: 词汇；某学科的词语总汇

entries.definition: all the words known or used in a language or field
entries.definitionCN: 词汇；词汇量

entries.definition: a reference book that lists words and explains them
entries.definitionCN: 词典；字典

normalIntro.en: Glossary is a gathering of glosses: the word adds -ary, a suffix for a collection, to the note word gloss.
normalIntro.cn: glossary 是注释的汇集：它在注释词 gloss 后面加了表示「汇集」的后缀 -ary。

normal.en: Glossary and gloss share a root: a glossary is a gathering of glosses.
normal.cn: glossary 与 gloss 同根：术语表就是注释的汇集。

normal.en: The -ary ending marks a collection, as in a library or a glossary.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ary 标记「汇集」，如同 library 与 glossary。

normal.en: A glossary sits at the back of a book, where a reader looks last.
normal.cn: 术语表待在书末，是读者最后翻到的地方。

normal.en: Glossarial is the adjective, and a glossarist writes glosses.
normal.cn: glossarial 是形容词，glossarist 是写注释的人。

normal.en: Compare vocabulary: a glossary is a selected list, not a whole word stock.
normal.cn: 对比 vocabulary：glossary 是挑选出来的清单，不是全部词汇。

abstract.en: See the last pages of a book filled with short alphabetized entries.
abstract.cn: 想象书末几页排满按字母排序的短词条。

abstract.en: See a shelf where each subject keeps its own small dictionary.
abstract.cn: 想象一排书架，每个学科都放着自己的小词典。

abstract.en: See an old manuscript with notes crowding the margins.
abstract.cn: 想象一份古旧手稿，页边挤满了注释。

examples.en: The glossary at the back explains each term.
examples.cn: 书后的术语表解释了每个术语。

examples.en: Our teacher asked us to build a glossary of new words.
examples.cn: 老师让我们编一份新词术语表。

examples.en: Both glossaries list the same scientific terms.
examples.cn: 两份术语表列出了相同的科学术语。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「格罗萨瑞」——书后一格格排好的术语，像抽屉里的标签；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 glōssa（舌头；语言；难解之词）→ 拉丁语 glossa（注释）→ 中世纪拉丁语 glossarium（注释汇编）→ 英语 glossary（术语表）。词根核心是把难词一条条解释清楚。

sensesIntro.en: Glossary starts as a collection of notes on hard words, becomes a list at the end of a book, and widens into a subject dictionary or a learner word list.
sensesIntro.cn: glossary 最初是难词注释的汇集，后来成为书末的词表，又扩展到学科词典与学习用词表。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small alphabet of hard words standing at the back of a book, each with its explanation.
core.cn: 核心意象：书末一小片按字母站好的难词，每个词后面跟着解释。

branches.en: The book-end list is the everyday sense of glossary.
branches.cn: 书末词表是 glossary 的日常义项。

branches.en: A subject reference work is the expanded sense.
branches.cn: 学科工具书是扩展后的义项。

branches.en: A collection of notes on an old text is the historical sense.
branches.cn: 对古旧文本的注释汇编是历史义项。

branches.en: A learner word list is the classroom sense.
branches.cn: 学习用难词表是课堂义项。

branches.en: Both a book-end list and a subject dictionary gather terms with definitions.
branches.cn: 书末词表与学科词典都把术语和释义汇集在一起。

intro.en: Glossary belongs to the gloss family: Greek glōssa, Latin glossa and glossarium, with English gloss and glossarial around it.
intro.cn: glossary 属于 gloss 词族：希腊语 glōssa、拉丁语 glossa 与 glossarium，周围还有英语 gloss 与 glossarial。

latinIntro.en: Latin glossa means an explanatory note, and glossarium means a collection of such notes.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 glossa 意为解释性注释，glossarium 意为这类注释的汇集。

items.example: Glōssa is the oldest source of the family.
items.exampleCN: glōssa 是这个词族最古老的源头。

items.example: Glossa gave English the note sense of gloss.
items.exampleCN: glossa 给英语的 gloss 送来了注释义。

items.example: Glossarium is the direct parent of glossary.
items.exampleCN: glossarium 是 glossary 的直接前身。

items.meaning: a list of terms with meanings
items.example: Glossary keeps the collection sense.
items.exampleCN: glossary 保留了「汇集」的含义。

items.example: Gloss is the short base word.
items.exampleCN: gloss 是简短的基础词。

items.example: Glossarial describes glossary material.
items.exampleCN: glossarial 描述与术语表有关的材料。

items.example: A glossarist collects and explains hard words.
items.exampleCN: glossarist 收集并解释难词。

items.example: The suffix -ary forms glossary.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ary 构成 glossary。

items.example: The suffix -ial forms glossarial.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ial 构成 glossarial。

definition_zh: 有光泽的；光滑的；光面的；浮华的；光面照片
definition_en: smooth and shiny, or printed on smooth shiny paper
core_image: 灯光下一层均匀的亮膜，摸上去滑得没有阻力
scene: 新杂志刚从塑料袋里拿出来，封面反着灯的光。The glossy cover caught the light as she opened the magazine.
sceneCN: 这里 glossy 是「有光泽的；光面的」（第 1 个义项：表面光滑并反光）；句意是她翻开杂志时，光面的封面反着灯光。

pos.zh: 有光泽的；光滑的；光面的；浮华的
光面照片；光面印刷品

derivatives.zh: 基础名词，义为「光泽；光亮表面」
由 glossy 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「光泽度」
由 glossy 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「光亮地」

senses.title: Smooth and shiny
senses.definition: smooth and bright, with a surface that reflects light
senses.definitionCN: 表面光滑明亮、能够反光的
senses.example: Her hair looked glossy after the treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 护理之后她的头发显得很有光泽。
senses.why: The shine word gloss plus -y makes an adjective for a surface that reflects light.
senses.whyCN: 表示光亮的 gloss 加形容词后缀 -y，就构成描述反光表面的形容词。

senses.title: Printed on shiny paper
senses.definition: printed on smooth shiny paper, so that pictures look bright and clear
senses.definitionCN: 印在光滑亮纸上，使图片显得明亮清晰的
senses.example: The brochure was printed on glossy paper.
senses.exampleCN: 这本宣传册用光面纸印刷。
senses.why: Paper makers gave the shine a technical use: a glossy surface takes ink sharply.
senses.whyCN: 造纸者把这种光亮用到工艺上：光面能更锐利地承载油墨。

senses.title: Showy but shallow
senses.definition: attractive in a superficial way, with more style than substance
senses.definitionCN: 外表诱人却缺乏实质，风格多于内容的
senses.example: The film offers a glossy version of country life.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片把乡村生活拍得光鲜而浮浅。
senses.why: A shiny surface hides what lies beneath, so glossy came to mean outwardly attractive and shallow.
senses.whyCN: 光亮的表面会遮住下面的东西，于是 glossy 引申为外表诱人而内里浮浅。

senses.title: A shiny photograph
senses.definition: a photograph printed on smooth shiny paper
senses.definitionCN: 印在光滑亮纸上的照片
senses.example: The magazine was full of glossies of film stars.
senses.exampleCN: 那本杂志里满是用光面纸印的影星照片。
senses.why: The adjective became a noun for a picture printed on shiny paper.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词转化为名词，专指印在光面纸上的照片。

intro.en: Glossy is gloss in its shine sense plus -y. The shine gloss is of uncertain northern origin and is unrelated to the note gloss from Greek.
intro.cn: glossy 是「光亮」义的 gloss 加后缀 -y 构成。光亮的 gloss 来源不确定，一般认为出自北方语言，与希腊语来源的注释词 gloss 无关。

items.en: The shine gloss appears in the sixteenth century, perhaps from Scandinavian or Low German.
