items.cn: 表示光亮的 gloss 在十六世纪出现，可能来自斯堪的纳维亚语或低地德语。

items.en: English adds -y to gloss and forms glossy, first for bright surfaces.
items.cn: 英语给 gloss 加上 -y 构成 glossy，最初描述明亮的表面。

items.en: Glossy extends to hair, paint and varnish that reflect light.
items.cn: glossy 的用法扩展到会反光的头发、油漆与清漆。

items.en: Glossy paper and glossy photographs spread with cheap colour printing.
items.cn: 随着廉价彩色印刷普及，光面纸与光面照片流行起来。

items.en: The glossy magazine style makes glossy mean showy and shallow.
items.cn: 光鲜杂志的风格使 glossy 引申为浮华而浅薄。

items.en: The plural noun glossies names shiny photographs.
items.cn: 复数名词 glossies 专指光面照片。

note.en: The first group gathers the shine family of gloss; the second gathers words for smooth bright surfaces.
note.cn: 第一组收 gloss 的光亮词族，第二组收表示光滑明亮表面的词。

entries.definition: a shine on a surface
entries.definitionCN: 光泽；光亮表面（glossy 的基础词）

entries.definition: the quality of being shiny
entries.definitionCN: 光泽度（由 glossy 加 -ness 构成）

entries.definition: in a shiny, smooth way
entries.definitionCN: 光亮地；光滑地（由 glossy 加 -ly 构成）

entries.definition: bright because it reflects light
entries.definitionCN: 闪亮的；有光泽的

entries.definition: smooth, shiny and elegant in shape
entries.definitionCN: 光滑亮泽而造型优雅的

entries.definition: shining softly, especially of hair or metal
entries.definitionCN: 有柔和光泽的（尤指头发或金属）

normalIntro.en: Glossy is gloss plus -y: the noun for shine turned into an adjective for anything that reflects light.
normalIntro.cn: glossy 就是 gloss 加 -y：表示光泽的名词变成描述反光之物的形容词。

normal.en: Glossy is gloss plus -y: the noun for shine turned into an adjective.
normal.cn: glossy 是 gloss 加 -y：表示光泽的名词变成了形容词。

normal.en: Glossy paper is smooth and reflects light, so photos look sharper.
normal.cn: 光面纸光滑反光，所以照片显得更清晰。

normal.en: Glossiness is the noun, and glossily is the adverb.
normal.cn: glossiness 是名词，glossily 是副词。

normal.en: A glossy magazine looks rich and smooth, which is why glossy also means showy.
normal.cn: 光鲜杂志显得富丽光滑，所以 glossy 也有浮华之义。

normal.en: Compare shiny: shiny is everyday, while glossy often describes manufactured surfaces.
normal.cn: 对比 shiny：shiny 更日常，glossy 常描述加工过的表面。

abstract.en: Imagine lamp light sliding across a varnished table.
abstract.cn: 想象灯光滑过刷了清漆的桌面。

abstract.en: Imagine a magazine cover that mirrors the room.
abstract.cn: 想象一张能映出房间的杂志封面。

abstract.en: Imagine a smooth cover with dull pages underneath.
abstract.cn: 想象光滑的封面下藏着暗淡的内页。

examples.en: The table had a glossy finish.
examples.cn: 桌面有一层亮面效果。

examples.en: She bought a glossy magazine at the airport.
examples.cn: 她在机场买了一本光鲜杂志。

examples.en: His glossy hair shone under the lamp.
examples.cn: 他有光泽的头发在灯下闪光。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「哥老西」——表面光得能照见人影；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 光亮义的 gloss（十六世纪出现，来源不确定，一般认为来自斯堪的纳维亚语或低地德语）加形容词后缀 -y，构成 glossy（有光泽的）。另有同形的 gloss（注释）来自希腊语 glōssa，与光亮义无关。

sensesIntro.en: Glossy begins with a shiny surface, passes to shiny paper and pictures, and ends with the idea of a showy surface that hides depth.
sensesIntro.cn: glossy 从反光的表面出发，转到光面纸与光面照片，最后引申为掩盖深度的浮华外表。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a smooth coat of shine lying on paper, hair or paint.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层光滑的亮膜覆在纸面、头发或油漆上。

branches.en: The basic adjective names any surface that reflects light.
branches.cn: 基本形容词义指任何反光的表面。

branches.en: Shiny paper and photographs are the commercial sense.
branches.cn: 光面纸与光面照片是商业义项。

branches.en: A showy style that hides depth is the figurative sense.
branches.cn: 掩盖深度的浮华风格是比喻义项。

branches.en: A photograph on shiny paper is the noun sense.
branches.cn: 印在光面纸上的照片是名词义项。

branches.en: A real shine and a showy manner both depend on what shows on the surface.
branches.cn: 真实的光泽与浮华的做派都取决于表面呈现。

intro.en: Glossy is the adjective of gloss in its shine sense, with glossiness and glossily built from it; the note gloss is a separate homonym.
intro.cn: glossy 是「光亮」义的 gloss 的形容词，又由它构成 glossiness 与 glossily；注释义的 gloss 则是同形异源词。

latinIntro.en: The shine word has no Latin source; Latin glossa and Greek glōssa belong to the unrelated note word.
latinIntro.cn: 光亮的这个词没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 glossa 与希腊语 glōssa 属于无关的注释词。

items.example: Gloss is the base of glossy.
items.exampleCN: gloss 是 glossy 的基础词。

items.example: The suffix -y changes gloss into glossy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 把 gloss 变成 glossy。

items.example: Glossy describes a reflecting surface.
items.exampleCN: glossy 描述反光的表面。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms glossiness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 glossiness。

items.example: Glossiness measures how much light a surface reflects.
items.exampleCN: glossiness 衡量表面反射多少光。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms glossily.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 glossily。

items.example: Glossily describes how a surface shines.
items.exampleCN: glossily 描述表面如何发光。

items.example: High-gloss paint gives a mirror-like finish.
items.exampleCN: 高光泽漆能做出镜面般的效果。

items.example: The note gloss is a homonym, not the source of glossy.
items.exampleCN: 注释义的 gloss 是同形异源词，不是 glossy 的来源。

definition_zh: 谷氨酸盐；谷氨酸酯；谷氨酸（神经递质）
definition_en: a salt or ester of glutamic acid, or the amino acid itself when it acts as a neurotransmitter
core_image: 一粒带电荷的小分子，越过缝隙把兴奋传给下一个细胞
scene: 实验室的屏幕上，一条神经信号曲线突然升高。Glutamate is the chemical behind that sudden rise.
sceneCN: 这里 glutamate 是「谷氨酸（神经递质）」（第 3 个义项：大脑中的主要兴奋性递质）；句意：实验室屏幕上那条突然升高的信号曲线，正是谷氨酸在起作用。

pos.zh: 谷氨酸盐；谷氨酸酯；谷氨酸

derivatives.zh: 由 glutamate 去掉 -ate 再加 -ic 构成，义为「谷氨酸的」
由谷氨酸词根加 -amine 构成，义为「谷氨酰胺」
由 glutamate 加 -ergic 构成，义为「谷氨酸能的」
由 glutamine 加 -ase 构成，义为「谷氨酰胺酶」

senses.title: A salt or ester of glutamic acid
senses.definition: a salt or ester formed from glutamic acid
senses.definitionCN: 由谷氨酸形成的盐或酯
senses.example: The chemist prepared a glutamate for the buffer solution.
senses.exampleCN: 化学家为缓冲液制备了一种谷氨酸盐。
senses.why: The suffix -ate names salts and esters in chemistry, so the word first labels a compound.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ate 在化学中表示盐或酯，所以这个词最先指一类化合物。

senses.title: The ionized amino acid
senses.definition: the form of glutamic acid that carries a negative charge at normal body pH
senses.definitionCN: 在正常体液酸碱度下带负电荷的谷氨酸形态
senses.example: Cells take up glutamate to build proteins.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞摄取谷氨酸来合成蛋白质。
senses.why: In body fluids the acid loses a proton, and the resulting anion is called glutamate.
senses.whyCN: 在体液中谷氨酸失去一个质子，形成的阴离子就叫谷氨酸。

senses.title: The brain signal molecule
senses.definition: the main excitatory neurotransmitter in the nervous system
senses.definitionCN: 神经系统中主要的兴奋性神经递质
senses.example: Glutamate carries most of the fast excitatory signals.
senses.exampleCN: 谷氨酸传递大多数快速兴奋信号。
senses.why: Because glutamate excites neurons, it became the central chemical messenger of the brain.
senses.whyCN: 由于谷氨酸能兴奋神经元，它成为大脑中最核心的化学信使。

senses.title: The source of savoury taste
senses.definition: glutamate as the molecule that gives food its savoury umami taste
senses.definitionCN: 作为赋予食物鲜味的分子
senses.example: Tomatoes and cheese are rich in natural glutamate.
senses.exampleCN: 番茄和奶酪富含天然谷氨酸。
senses.why: Glutamate is the taste signal behind umami, which is why cooks add it to food.
senses.whyCN: 谷氨酸是鲜味背后的味觉信号，所以厨师会把它加入食物。

senses.title: A metabolic hub
senses.definition: a key intermediate that moves nitrogen between amino acids and the energy cycle
senses.definitionCN: 在氨基酸与能量循环之间转运氮的关键中间产物
senses.example: The liver uses glutamate to move nitrogen safely.
senses.exampleCN: 肝脏利用谷氨酸安全地转运氮。
senses.why: Its central place in amino acid chemistry makes glutamate a hub for nitrogen traffic.
senses.whyCN: 谷氨酸在氨基酸化学中的中心位置，使它成为氮流转的枢纽。

intro.en: Glutamate is built from Latin gluten, glue, through German chemistry: glutamic acid was named in 1866 for its wheat source.
intro.cn: glutamate 由拉丁语 gluten（胶）经德语化学构词而来，谷氨酸于 1866 年因源自小麦面筋而得名。

items.en: Gluten means glue, the sticky protein of wheat.
items.cn: gluten 意为胶，指小麦中黏性的蛋白质。

items.en: Glutaminsäure is coined from gluten and the acid suffix.
items.cn: 1866 年，Glutaminsäure 由 gluten 与酸类后缀构成。

items.en: Glutamic acid enters chemical English.
items.cn: glutamic acid 进入英语化学文献。

items.en: Glutamate names the salt, the ester, and later the amino acid in cells.
items.cn: glutamate 指盐、酯，后来也指细胞中的谷氨酸。

items.en: Neurobiology makes glutamate the best known excitatory transmitter.
items.cn: 神经生物学让谷氨酸成为最著名的兴奋性递质。

items.en: Food science links glutamate to umami and to monosodium glutamate.
items.cn: 食品科学把谷氨酸与鲜味及味精联系起来。

note.en: Glutamate is the salt form of glutamic acid, sitting in a family of amino acid and brain signal words.
note.cn: glutamate 是谷氨酸的盐形式，处在氨基酸与脑信号词的词族中。

entries.definition: relating to glutamic acid
entries.definitionCN: 谷氨酸的

entries.definition: an amino acid related to glutamate
entries.definitionCN: 与谷氨酸同源的氨基酸「谷氨酰胺」

entries.definition: using glutamate as a neurotransmitter
entries.definitionCN: 以谷氨酸为递质的

entries.definition: a chemical that carries signals between nerve cells
entries.definitionCN: 在神经细胞间传递信号的化学物质

entries.definition: another excitatory amino acid transmitter
entries.definitionCN: 另一种兴奋性氨基酸递质「天冬氨酸」

entries.definition: the savoury taste that glutamate produces
entries.definitionCN: 谷氨酸产生的鲜味

normalIntro.en: Glutamate is a working molecule: a salt in the lab, a signal in the brain, a taste in food.
normalIntro.cn: glutamate 是一个干活的分子：实验室里是盐，大脑里是信号，食物里是味道。

normal.en: Glutamate is the anion of glutamic acid.
normal.cn: glutamate 是谷氨酸的阴离子。

normal.en: Monosodium glutamate is the white powder sold as a flavour enhancer.
normal.cn: monosodium glutamate 就是作为增味剂出售的白色粉末。

normal.en: Glutamate receptors sit on the surface of nerve cells.
normal.cn: 谷氨酸受体位于神经细胞表面。

normal.en: Too much glutamate can overexcite a neuron.
normal.cn: 谷氨酸过多会使神经元过度兴奋。

normal.en: Compare glutamine: one letter and one amide group separate the two amino acids.
normal.cn: 对比 glutamine：一个字母和一个酰胺基把两种氨基酸区分开。

abstract.en: Picture a grain of salt dissolving into a clear solution.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒盐溶进清澈的溶液。

abstract.en: See a tiny negative charge sitting on the acid molecule.
abstract.cn: 想象酸分子上带着一个小小的负电荷。

abstract.en: Imagine a spark jumping between two nerve endings.
abstract.cn: 想象一点火花在两个神经末梢之间跳跃。

examples.en: Monosodium glutamate adds a savoury note to soups and snacks.
examples.cn: 味精给汤和零食增添鲜味。

examples.en: Glutamate is released at most excitatory synapses in the brain.
examples.cn: 大脑中大多数兴奋性突触都会释放谷氨酸。

examples.en: Doctors measured glutamate levels in the spinal fluid.
examples.cn: 医生测量了脊髓液中的谷氨酸水平。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「谷路特美」——记成「谷」物里的鲜味「特美」，只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 gluten（胶、黏合物）→ 德语 Glutaminsäure（1866 年）→ 英语 glutamic acid → glutamate；核心义「来自面筋的氨基酸及其盐」。

sensesIntro.en: Glutamate moves from a chemistry salt to the amino acid in cells, then to the brain signal, the taste of umami, and a metabolic hub.
sensesIntro.cn: glutamate 从化学上的盐，走到细胞里的氨基酸，再到大脑信号、鲜味来源与代谢枢纽。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tiny charged molecule that carries excitement across a gap.
core.cn: 核心意象：一粒带电荷的小分子，把兴奋送过缝隙。

branches.en: The chemistry sense names a salt or ester.
branches.cn: 化学义项指盐或酯。

branches.en: The amino acid sense names the charged form inside cells.
branches.cn: 氨基酸义项指细胞内的带电形态。

branches.en: The neuroscience sense names the excitatory transmitter.
branches.cn: 神经科学义项指兴奋性递质。

branches.en: The food sense names the source of umami.
branches.cn: 食品义项指鲜味来源。

branches.en: The metabolic sense names a nitrogen hub.
branches.cn: 代谢义项指氮转运枢纽。

intro.en: Glutamate is a Latin chemistry word: gluten gave the root, and -ate marks the salt.
intro.cn: glutamate 是一个拉丁语源的化学词：gluten 提供词根，-ate 标记盐类。

latinIntro.en: Latin gluten means glue, and glutamic acid was first isolated from wheat gluten.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gluten 意为胶，谷氨酸最早正是从小麦面筋中分离出来的。

items.example: Gluten gives the sticky feel of dough.
items.exampleCN: gluten 使面团有黏性。

items.example: The suffix -ic turns gluten into glutamic.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ic 把 gluten 变成 glutamic。

items.meaning: relating to gluten or glutamic acid
items.example: Glutamic acid is the parent acid.
items.exampleCN: glutamic acid 是母体酸。

items.example: Acid and salt form a pair.
items.exampleCN: 酸与盐构成一对。

items.example: The suffix -ate marks a salt.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ate 标记盐类。

items.meaning: a salt or ester of glutamic acid
items.example: Glutamate is the name of the salt.
items.exampleCN: glutamate 是这种盐的名称。

items.meaning: an amino acid made from glutamate
items.meaningCN: 由谷氨酸生成的氨基酸「谷氨酰胺」
items.example: Glutamine carries nitrogen in the blood.
items.exampleCN: glutamine 在血液中运送氮。

items.example: Glutamatergic neurons excite the cortex.
items.exampleCN: 谷氨酸能神经元兴奋大脑皮层。

items.example: Glutaminase releases glutamate in cells.
items.exampleCN: glutaminase 在细胞中释放谷氨酸。

definition_zh: 善意；好心；商誉；友好关系
definition_en: kindly feeling toward others, or the good reputation and friendly relations that such feeling creates
core_image: 一只在别人开口之前就伸出的援助之手
scene: 街角的旧书店里，店主把一本旧书留给熟客，却没有收钱。Goodwill is the reason he keeps the book aside without payment.
sceneCN: 这里 goodwill 是「善意；好心」（第 1 个义项：对他人的友善与乐于相助之情）；句意：店主把书留在一旁不收钱，正是出于善意。

pos.zh: 善意；好心；商誉；友好关系

derivatives.zh: 由 goodwill 加 -ed 构成，义为「怀有善意的」
由 goodwill 与 gesture 复合，义为「善意之举」
由 goodwill 与 ambassador 复合，义为「亲善大使」

senses.title: Kindly feeling
senses.definition: a friendly and helpful feeling toward other people
senses.definitionCN: 对他人的友善与乐于相助之情
senses.example: She helped the new neighbour out of sheer goodwill.
senses.exampleCN: 她纯粹出于善意帮助了新邻居。
senses.why: The word joins good and will, so it names a will that wishes others well.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 good 与 will 组合，指希望别人好的心意。

senses.title: The reputation of a business
senses.definition: the good reputation and customer loyalty that a business has built up
senses.definitionCN: 企业积累起来的良好声誉与顾客忠诚
senses.example: The shop lost years of goodwill after the scandal.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻之后，这家店失去了多年积累的商誉。
senses.why: A business treats customer affection as property, so friendly feeling becomes an asset called goodwill.
senses.whyCN: 企业把顾客的好感当作财产，于是友善之情变成一项叫商誉的资产。

senses.title: An accounting asset
senses.definition: the amount paid for a company above the fair value of its net assets
senses.definitionCN: 收购一家公司时超出其净资产公允价值的付款
senses.example: The takeover created a large goodwill entry on the books.
senses.exampleCN: 这次收购在账上形成了一笔巨额商誉。
senses.why: Accountants needed a name for the extra price paid for reputation, and goodwill already meant good name.
senses.whyCN: 会计需要为购买声誉多付的价款命名，而 goodwill 本就有好名声之意。

senses.title: A friendly gesture
senses.definition: an act or offer that shows friendly intention, often to keep relations smooth
senses.definitionCN: 显示友好意图的举动或提议，常用来维持关系顺畅
senses.example: The company offered a free repair as a goodwill gesture.
senses.exampleCN: 公司以免费维修作为善意之举。
senses.why: Concrete acts express the abstract feeling, so a gesture made in good will takes the name goodwill.
senses.whyCN: 具体行动表达抽象情感，所以出于善意做出的举动也以 goodwill 为名。

senses.title: Friendly relations between groups
senses.definition: a state of friendly cooperation between countries, groups, or communities
senses.definitionCN: 国家、团体或社区之间友好合作的状态
senses.example: The treaty was signed in a spirit of goodwill.
senses.exampleCN: 条约在友好精神中签署。
senses.why: When goodwill is shared by whole groups, it becomes the political sense of friendly relations.
senses.whyCN: 当善意被整个群体共享，它就变成友好关系这一政治义项。

intro.en: Goodwill is an English compound of good and will, first recorded in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: goodwill 是 good 与 will 的英语复合词，最早见于十九世纪。

items.en: God means good, and will means wish or desire.
items.cn: god 意为好，will 意为意愿或愿望。

items.en: Good and will often appear side by side as separate words.
items.cn: 在中古英语中，good 与 will 常作为两个词并排出现。

items.en: Goodwill is written as one noun for kindly feeling.
items.cn: 十九世纪，goodwill 写成一个名词，指善意。

items.en: Commerce adds the sense of the good name of a business.
items.cn: 商业用法又加上企业好名声这一义项。

items.en: Accounting makes goodwill a measurable asset.
items.cn: 会计学把商誉变成可计量的资产。

items.en: Diplomacy uses goodwill for friendly relations between states.
items.cn: 外交用法以 goodwill 指国家间的友好关系。

note.en: Goodwill is a transparent English compound, close to its two parts and to words for kindness and reputation.
note.cn: goodwill 是一个意思透明的英语复合词，与它的两个组成部分以及表示善心、声誉的词相邻。

entries.definition: kind, virtuous, or morally right
entries.definitionCN: 善良的；好的

entries.definition: the power of choosing or wishing
entries.definitionCN: 意愿；意志

entries.definition: having good intentions
entries.definitionCN: 怀有善意的

entries.definition: kindness and generosity toward others
entries.definitionCN: 仁慈；善心

entries.definition: the voluntary giving of help to those in need
entries.definitionCN: 慈善；施舍

entries.definition: a warm and friendly attitude
entries.definitionCN: 友好；亲切

normalIntro.en: Goodwill is good will: a wish for another person to fare well, and the reputation that wish earns.
normalIntro.cn: goodwill 就是 good will：希望别人过得好的一份心意，以及这份心意换来的好名声。

normal.en: Goodwill is written as one word, good plus will.
normal.cn: goodwill 写成一个词，由 good 加 will 构成。

normal.en: A goodwill gesture costs little but buys trust.
normal.cn: 善意之举花费不多，却能换来信任。

normal.en: Companies record goodwill when they pay extra for a good name.
normal.cn: 企业为良好名声多付钱时，就把商誉记入账上。

normal.en: Goodwill between neighbours keeps a street peaceful.
normal.cn: 邻里之间的善意让一条街保持安宁。

normal.en: Compare good will: the noun is one word, the phrase means the same feeling.
normal.cn: 对比 good will：名词写作一个词，短语也表示同样的心意。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching out before anyone asks for help.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在别人开口求助之前就伸了出去。

abstract.en: See a shopkeeper greeting regular customers by name.
abstract.cn: 想象店主叫着老顾客的名字打招呼。

abstract.en: Imagine a ledger line labelled with a good name.
abstract.cn: 想象账本上有一行写着好名声。

examples.en: She greeted every guest with genuine goodwill.
examples.cn: 她以真诚的善意迎接每一位客人。

examples.en: The brand has built decades of goodwill among local shoppers.
examples.cn: 这个品牌在当地顾客中积累了数十年的好感。

examples.en: The two countries exchanged gifts as a sign of goodwill.
examples.cn: 两国互赠礼物以示友好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「古德威尔」——待人「古」道、有「德」，自然有「威」信，这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: good（好）+ will（意愿）→ goodwill；核心义「希望别人好的心意」，再引申为声誉、商誉与友好关系。

sensesIntro.en: Goodwill begins as a kindly wish, becomes a business reputation and an accounting asset, then a friendly gesture and a state of friendly relations.
sensesIntro.cn: goodwill 从一份善意的祝愿开始，变成企业声誉与会计上的商誉，再变成友好举动与友好关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open hand offering help before it is asked for.
core.cn: 核心意象：在别人开口之前就伸出的援助之手。

branches.en: The kindly feeling is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 友善之情是日常义项。

branches.en: The business reputation is the commercial sense.
branches.cn: 企业声誉是商业义项。

branches.en: The accounting asset is the technical sense.
branches.cn: 会计资产是技术义项。

branches.en: The friendly gesture is the action sense.
branches.cn: 友好举动是行动义项。

branches.en: Friendly relations are the collective sense.
branches.cn: 友好关系是集体义项。

intro.en: Goodwill is an English compound of good and will, with a transparent modern meaning.
intro.cn: goodwill 是 good 与 will 的英语复合词，现代含义一目了然。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor; good and will both descend from Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语祖先，good 与 will 都来自古英语。

items.example: Good adds the favourable meaning.
items.exampleCN: good 加上「好」的含义。

items.example: Will supplies the wishing part.
items.exampleCN: will 提供「意愿」这一部分。

items.example: Goodwill joins the two words.
items.exampleCN: goodwill 把这两个词合在一起。

items.example: Goodwilled neighbours help each other.
items.exampleCN: 怀有善意的邻居互相帮助。

items.example: A small gift can be a goodwill gesture.
items.exampleCN: 一件小礼物可以是善意之举。

items.meaning: a public figure who promotes friendly relations
items.example: The singer serves as a goodwill ambassador.
items.exampleCN: 这位歌手担任亲善大使。

items.meaning: a write-down of the value of goodwill
items.example: The company reported a goodwill impairment.
items.exampleCN: 公司报告了一笔商誉减值。

items.example: Ill will is the opposite of goodwill.
items.exampleCN: ill will 是 goodwill 的反面。

definition_zh: 大猩猩；壮汉；打手；（说一不二的）巨头
definition_en: a very large strong African ape, or a person compared to such an animal for size or power
core_image: 一头银背大猩猩挺胸而立，像森林里一堵会动的肌肉之墙
scene: 雨林深处，一只银背大猩猩拨开藤蔓，护住身后的族群。The gorilla beats its chest and the whole troop falls silent.
sceneCN: 这里 gorilla 是「大猩猩」（第 1 个义项：非洲的大型灵长类动物）；句意：那只大猩猩捶打胸口，整群猩猩立刻安静下来。

pos.zh: 大猩猩；壮汉；打手；巨头

collocations.zh: 人人避而不谈的明显问题

derivatives.zh: 由 gorilla 加 -ine 构成，义为「大猩猩的；大猩猩似的」
由 gorilla 与 like 复合，义为「像大猩猩的」
由 gorilla 加 -oid 构成，义为「形似大猩猩的」

senses.title: The African ape
senses.definition: a very large, strong ape that lives in the forests of Africa
senses.definitionCN: 生活在非洲森林中的大型强壮猿类
senses.example: A young gorilla clung to its mother in the trees.
senses.exampleCN: 一只幼年大猩猩在树上紧紧攀着母亲。
senses.why: The name came from a Greek word for a hairy people, and explorers gave it to the great ape.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字来自希腊语中对长毛人群的称呼，探险者把它给了这种大型猿类。

senses.title: A large strong man
senses.definition: a big, strong, and often aggressive man, especially one hired to protect or intimidate
senses.definitionCN: 高大强壮、常常带攻击性的男人，尤指受雇保护或恐吓他人者
senses.example: Two gorillas in dark suits guarded the door.
senses.exampleCN: 两个穿深色西装的壮汉守在门口。
senses.why: Because the animal is powerful and imposing, people compare muscular guards or thugs to it.
senses.whyCN: 因为这种动物强壮而威猛，人们就把肌肉发达的保镖或打手比作它。

senses.title: An unbeatable giant
senses.definition: a powerful person or organization that others are afraid to challenge
senses.definitionCN: 其他人不敢挑战的有权势者或机构
senses.example: The company became the eight-hundred-pound gorilla of the market.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司成了市场上说一不二的巨头。
senses.why: The saying about an eight-hundred-pound gorilla made the animal a symbol of unchecked power.
senses.whyCN: 关于「八百磅的大猩猩」的说法，让这种动物成为不受制约的权力的象征。

senses.title: The genus Gorilla
senses.definition: the taxonomic genus that contains the two African gorilla species
senses.definitionCN: 包含非洲两种大猩猩的分类学属
senses.example: The genus Gorilla split from other apes millions of years ago.
senses.exampleCN: 大猩猩属在数百万年前与其他猿类分化。
senses.why: Taxonomy needed a formal Latin name, so the common word also names the genus.
senses.whyCN: 分类学需要一个正式的拉丁名，于是这个常用词也用来命名该属。

senses.title: The obvious problem nobody mentions
senses.titleCN: 人人避而不谈的明显问题
senses.definition: an obvious difficulty or awkward fact that everyone present avoids discussing
senses.definitionCN: 在场者都心知肚明却避而不谈的明显困难或尴尬事实
senses.example: Cost overruns are the gorilla in the room at the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 成本超支是会上人人避而不谈的明显问题。
senses.why: The gorilla in the room is impossible to ignore, so the idiom names a problem everyone sees and avoids.
senses.whyCN: 房间里的猩猩无法被忽视，所以这个习语指人人都看见却回避的问题。

intro.en: Gorilla goes back to Greek Gorillai, a hairy people reported by the Carthaginian explorer Hanno, and was applied to the ape in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: gorilla 可追溯到希腊语 Gorillai，那是迦太基探险家汉诺记述的长毛人群，十九世纪这个词被用于这种猿类。

items.en: Gorillai names a tribe of hairy people in the account of Hanno.
items.cn: 在汉诺的航行记中，Gorillai 指一个长毛的部族。

items.en: The Greek form may come from an African language, but the source is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个希腊词形可能来自某种非洲语言，但来源不确定。

items.en: Naturalists Latinize the name as Gorilla for the newly described ape.
items.cn: 博物学家把这个名字拉丁化为 Gorilla，用来称呼这种新描述的猿。

items.en: Gorilla enters English after the ape is described in 1847.
items.cn: 1847 年这种猿被描述之后，gorilla 进入英语。

items.en: The animal name grows figurative senses of strength and menace.
items.cn: 动物名逐渐引申出强壮与威吓的比喻义。

items.en: The gorilla in the room adds the sense of an ignored problem.
items.cn: 「房间里的猩猩」这一说法又增添了被忽视的问题这一义项。

note.en: Gorilla is the great ape of central Africa, close to spelling twins and to other large primates.
note.cn: gorilla 是中部非洲的大型猿类，与几个拼写相近词以及其他大型灵长类相邻。

entries.definition: relating to gorillas
entries.definitionCN: 大猩猩的

entries.definition: a member of a small unofficial fighting group
entries.definitionCN: 游击队员；只是拼写与 gorilla 相近，词源不同

entries.definition: resembling a gorilla
entries.definitionCN: 形似大猩猩的

entries.definition: a large primate without a tail
entries.definitionCN: 猿；大型灵长类

entries.definition: a smaller intelligent African primate
entries.definitionCN: 黑猩猩

entries.definition: a large tree-dwelling ape of Southeast Asia
entries.definitionCN: 猩猩（东南亚的大型树栖猿类）

normalIntro.en: Gorilla is a giant ape with a borrowed name, and English uses it for size, power, and awkward silence.
normalIntro.cn: gorilla 是一种名字借来的巨型猿类，英语用它来指体型、权力和尴尬的沉默。

normal.en: Gorilla comes from a Greek name for a hairy tribe.
normal.cn: gorilla 来自希腊语中一个长毛部族之名。

normal.en: A silverback gorilla leads the troop.
normal.cn: 银背大猩猩率领整个群体。

normal.en: Mountain gorillas live in cool high forests.
normal.cn: 山地大猩猩生活在凉爽的高山森林里。

normal.en: The eight-hundred-pound gorilla does whatever it wants.
normal.cn: 八百磅的大猩猩想做什么就做什么。

normal.en: The gorilla in the room is the problem everyone avoids.
normal.cn: 房间里的猩猩就是人人都回避的问题。

abstract.en: See a huge shadow moving between the trees.
abstract.cn: 想象一个巨大的影子在树间移动。

abstract.en: Picture broad shoulders filling a doorway.
abstract.cn: 想象宽厚的肩膀堵住整个门口。

abstract.en: Imagine a giant sitting at the boardroom table.
abstract.cn: 想象一个巨人坐在会议桌旁。

examples.en: The gorilla lifted a branch as if it were a twig.
examples.cn: 那只大猩猩举起一根树枝，仿佛那只是细枝。

examples.en: A gorilla in a black suit stood beside the door.
examples.cn: 一个穿黑西装的壮汉站在门边。

examples.en: The overlooked budget is the gorilla in the room.
examples.cn: 被忽视的预算问题就是那个无人敢提的明显问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哥斯拉」——体型巨大、力气惊人，像电影里的巨兽，只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 Gorillai（长毛部族，来源不确定）→ 拉丁语 Gorilla → 英语 gorilla；核心义「非洲的大型猿类」，再引申指壮汉与巨头。

sensesIntro.en: Gorilla starts as the name of the African ape, then labels a strong man, an unbeatable giant, a taxonomic genus, and an obvious problem nobody mentions.
sensesIntro.cn: gorilla 先是非洲大型猿类的名字，再指壮汉、说一不二的巨头、分类学上的属，以及人人避而不谈的明显问题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a silverback standing chest-high, a wall of muscle in the forest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一头银背大猩猩挺胸而立，像森林里一堵肌肉筑成的墙。

branches.en: The animal sense is the original name.
branches.cn: 动物义项是这个名字的本义。

branches.en: The strong man sense borrows the animal build.
branches.cn: 壮汉义项借用了这种动物的体格。

branches.en: The giant sense borrows the animal power.
branches.cn: 巨头义项借用了这种动物的力量。

branches.en: The genus sense is the scientific use.
branches.cn: 属名义项是科学用法。

branches.en: The ignored problem sense comes from the room idiom.
branches.cn: 被忽视的问题义项来自「房间里的猩猩」这一习语。

intro.en: Gorilla is a borrowed name from Greek, reshaped in Latin and English; its English family is mostly adjectives and compounds.
intro.cn: gorilla 是从希腊语借来的名字，经拉丁语与英语改造；它的英语词族主要是形容词与复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin scientific name Gorilla comes from Greek Gorillai, a word of uncertain origin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语学名 Gorilla 来自希腊语 Gorillai，其来源不确定。

items.example: Gorillai is the earliest traced form.
items.exampleCN: Gorillai 是最早可追溯的形式。

items.example: Latin fixes the scientific name Gorilla.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语确定了学名 Gorilla。

items.example: Gorilla names the animal in English.
items.exampleCN: gorilla 在英语中指这种动物。

items.example: The suffix -s forms gorillas.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -s 构成 gorillas。

items.example: Gorilline features appear in the skull.
items.exampleCN: 颅骨上可见大猩猩的特征。

items.example: A gorilla-like figure filled the stage.
items.exampleCN: 一个像大猩猩的身影占满了舞台。

items.example: The drawing shows a gorilloid face.
items.exampleCN: 这幅画呈现了一张形似大猩猩的脸。

items.example: The suffix -oid forms gorilloid.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -oid 构成 gorilloid。

definition_zh: 闲话；流言蜚语；爱说闲话的人；说闲话
definition_en: talk about the private lives of other people, often unkind or untrue, or a person who talks in this way
core_image: 井边围成一圈的邻居，压低声音交换别人的私事
scene: 午休时，几个人挤在茶水间低声议论新来的主管。The whole office was buzzing with gossip about the new manager.
sceneCN: 这里 gossip 是「流言、闲话」（第 1 个义项：关于他人私事的闲话）；句意：午休时，几个人挤在茶水间低声议论新来的主管。

pos.zh: 闲话；流言蜚语；爱说闲话的人
说闲话；传播流言

derivatives.zh: 动词 gossip 加表人后缀 -er，义为「爱传闲话的人」
名词 gossip 加形容词后缀 -y，义为「爱说闲话的；充满闲话的」
gossip 与 monger（商人）复合，义为「以散布流言为业的人」

senses.title: Idle talk about other people
senses.definition: talk or stories about the private lives of other people, often exaggerated, unkind, or untrue
senses.definitionCN: 关于他人私生活的闲话或传闻，常被夸大、刻薄或不实
senses.example: Gossip about the new neighbour spread through the street within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 关于新邻居的闲话一周之内就传遍了整条街。
senses.why: The Old English word named a godparent, a person bound to the family by faith, so the word began with intimate knowledge of other people and later named the talk such intimates exchanged.
senses.whyCN: 这个古英语词本指教父教母，即因信仰而与家庭结缘的人，所以词义起点是「对他人私事的亲近了解」，后来才指这种亲近者之间交换的话。

senses.title: A person who passes talk on
senses.definition: a person who habitually talks about the private lives of other people
senses.definitionCN: 习惯谈论他人私事的人
senses.example: She is the office gossip, and everyone knows it.
senses.exampleCN: 她是办公室里的闲话中心，这一点人人都知道。
senses.why: English first used the word for the companion who exchanged such talk, so the name of the person survived beside the name of the talk.
senses.whyCN: 英语最初用这个词指交换这类闲话的同伴，于是「人」的称呼与「话」的称呼并存了下来。

senses.title: To talk about other people
senses.definition: to talk about the private affairs of other people, especially when they are not present
senses.definitionCN: 议论他人的私事，尤指当事人不在场时
senses.example: The neighbours gossiped about the family for months.
senses.exampleCN: 邻居们议论这家人议论了好几个月。
senses.why: Once the noun meant idle talk, the verb simply named the act of producing it.
senses.whyCN: 名词一旦表示「闲话」，动词自然就表示制造闲话这个动作。

senses.title: To chat in a friendly way
senses.definition: in older use, to talk lightly and pleasantly with friends, without any suggestion of scandal
senses.definitionCN: 较早用法中指与朋友轻松愉快地聊天，不含丑闻色彩
senses.example: They gossiped by the fire until the candles burned low.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在炉边闲聊，直到蜡烛烧得只剩一点。
senses.why: The original companion sense kept a warm, neutral tone, so the verb could mean no more than passing the time in talk.
senses.whyCN: 原初的「同伴」义保留着温暖中性的语气，所以动词可以仅仅表示在闲谈中消磨时间。

senses.title: Personal news as entertainment
senses.definition: the reporting of personal and private news about famous people, printed or broadcast as entertainment
senses.definitionCN: 把名人的私事当作娱乐来报道的内容
senses.example: The wedding filled the gossip pages for a fortnight.
senses.exampleCN: 那场婚礼在八卦版上热闹了两个星期。
senses.why: Modern media turned the old habit of talk into a product, so gossip became a named section of newspapers and websites.
senses.whyCN: 现代媒体把古老的闲谈习惯变成了产品，于是 gossip 成了报纸与网站上固定的一个栏目。

intro.en: Gossip goes back to Old English godsibb, a godparent, formed from god and sibb, kinship; the sense moved from the baptismal sponsor to a close companion and then to the talk such companions exchanged.
intro.cn: gossip 可追溯到古英语 godsibb（教父教母），由 god（神）与 sibb（亲属关系）构成；词义从受洗担保人转为亲密同伴，再转指这类同伴交换的闲话。

items.en: Godsibb joins god, deity, and sibb, kinship, and names a baptismal sponsor.
items.cn: godsibb 由 god（神）与 sibb（亲属关系）合成，指受洗时的担保人，即教父或教母。

items.en: The form gossib keeps the sponsor sense and also means a close friend or companion.
items.cn: 中古英语形式 gossib 保留担保人之义，同时指密友或同伴。

items.en: The word is often used of the women who attended a birth, and of the talk they exchanged.
items.cn: 这个词常用来指陪产的女性友人，也指她们之间的交谈。

items.en: The meaning shifts from the person to the talk itself, idle stories about other people.
items.cn: 词义由人转向话本身，指关于他人的无根据传闻。

items.en: Modern English adds gossip column, celebrity gossip, and the verb to gossip.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了 gossip column、celebrity gossip 以及动词用法。

note.en: Gossip is the word for talk that runs from mouth to mouth, close to its own family of forms and to the ordinary words for rumour and chat.
note.cn: gossip 指口耳相传的闲话，与自身的词族形式相邻，也与表示传闻和闲聊的普通词相邻。

entries.definition: a person who often gossips
entries.definitionCN: 常传闲话的人

entries.definition: full of gossip, or fond of passing it on
entries.definitionCN: 充满闲话的；爱传闲话的

entries.definition: a fine thread of spider silk, or a very thin delicate material
entries.definitionCN: 蛛丝；极薄的织物——只是拼写与读音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: talk that may be untrue and spreads from person to person
entries.definitionCN: 传闻；谣言

entries.definition: light, continuous talk about unimportant things
entries.definitionCN: 闲聊；喋喋不休

entries.definition: trivial talk about other people, usually of little worth
entries.definitionCN: 无谓的闲话；碎嘴

normalIntro.en: Gossip carries a family history worth knowing: it began as a word for a godparent and only later came to mean idle talk.
normalIntro.cn: gossip 有一段值得知道的家族史：它最初指教父教母，后来才表示闲话。

normal.en: Old English godsibb, a godparent, is the ancestor of gossip.
normal.cn: 古英语 godsibb（教父教母）是 gossip 的前身。

normal.en: The noun and the verb share one spelling: gossip, gossiped, gossiping.
normal.cn: 名词与动词拼写相同：gossip、gossiped、gossiping。

normal.en: Spread gossip and office gossip are the everyday patterns.
normal.cn: spread gossip 与 office gossip 是日常搭配。

normal.en: Gossipy describes a person or a report full of such talk.
normal.cn: gossipy 形容爱传闲话的人，或充满闲话的报道。

normal.en: Compare rumour: a rumour is one unverified story, while gossip is the habit or the whole flow of such talk.
normal.cn: 对比 rumour：rumour 是一则未经证实的传闻，gossip 则是这种谈话的习惯或整体流动。

abstract.en: Picture a steaming kettle and two neighbours leaning close, voices low.
abstract.cn: 想象一壶冒着热气的水，两位邻居凑得很近，声音压得很低。

abstract.en: Picture one woman carrying a story from door to door like a basket of eggs.
abstract.cn: 想象一个女人像拎着一篮鸡蛋那样，把一则故事从一家带到另一家。

abstract.en: Picture a mouth passing a story on and a second mouth already repeating it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张嘴把故事传出去，另一张嘴已经在重复它了。

examples.en: Office gossip spread faster than the official memo.
examples.cn: 办公室闲话比正式通知传得还快。

examples.en: She gossiped about a colleague and regretted it the same afternoon.
examples.cn: 她议论了一位同事，当天下午就后悔了。

examples.en: The magazine is full of celebrity gossip and very little news.
examples.cn: 这本杂志满是名人八卦，真正的新闻却很少。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「锅四婆」——四个婆婆围着锅边，把邻居的事说了一遍又一遍；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 godsibb（教父教母）＝ god（神）＋ sibb（亲属关系），本义「因信仰结成的亲属」，后指密友，再由密友间的私语转指闲话。

sensesIntro.en: Gossip starts as the name of a person close to the family, moves to the talk such people exchanged, then splits into the talk, the person who spreads it, the act of spreading it, and the media form of it.
sensesIntro.cn: gossip 起初是与家庭亲近之人的称呼，转而指这类人之间的交谈，随后分化为闲话本身、传闲话的人、传闲话的动作，以及媒体上的八卦。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ring of neighbours whispering beside a well.
core.cn: 核心意象：井边围成一圈低声耳语的邻居。

branches.en: The talk itself is the central modern sense.
branches.cn: 闲话本身是核心的现代义项。

branches.en: The person who keeps such talk alive is named by the same word.
branches.cn: 维持这类闲话的人用同一个词来称呼。

branches.en: The verb names the act of producing the talk.
branches.cn: 动词表示制造这类闲话的行为。

branches.en: The old friendly sense survives as light, harmless chat.
branches.cn: 旧的友好义项留存为轻松无害的闲聊。

branches.en: Media gossip packages the central sense as entertainment.
branches.cn: 媒体八卦把核心义项包装成娱乐产品。

intro.en: Gossip is built from two Old English words, and English later added -er, -y, and the compound gossipmonger around it.
intro.cn: gossip 由两个古英语词合成，英语后来围绕它加上 -er、-y，并构成复合词 gossipmonger。

latinIntro.en: Gossip has no Latin root: it comes from Old English and the Germanic family, where sibb is related to German Sippe, a clan.
latinIntro.cn: gossip 没有拉丁词根：它来自古英语与日耳曼语族，其中的 sibb 与德语 Sippe（氏族）同源。

items.example: God forms the first part of godsibb.
items.exampleCN: god 构成 godsibb 的前半部分。

items.example: Sibb supplies the family meaning.
items.exampleCN: sibb 提供「亲属」这一层含义。

items.example: Godsibb is the direct ancestor of gossip.
items.exampleCN: godsibb 是 gossip 的直接前身。

items.meaning: a close companion, then idle talk
items.example: Gossip carries both senses into modern English.
items.exampleCN: gossip 把两种含义带进现代英语。

items.example: The suffix -er forms gossiper.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 gossiper。

items.example: Gossiper names the person, not the talk.
items.exampleCN: gossiper 指人，不指话。

items.example: The suffix -y forms gossipy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成 gossipy。

items.meaningCN: 爱传闲话的；充满闲话的
items.example: Gossipy describes a tone or a person.
items.exampleCN: gossipy 可形容语气，也可形容人。

items.example: Monger means a trader, so a gossipmonger trades in talk.
items.exampleCN: monger 意为商人，所以 gossipmonger 是以闲话为货的人。

items.meaning: a newspaper feature about famous people
items.meaningCN: 报纸上的名人八卦专栏
items.example: A gossip column turns talk into a printed product.
items.exampleCN: gossip column 把闲话变成印刷品。

definition_zh: 语法学家；语法专家；语法书作者
definition_en: a person who studies, teaches, or writes about grammar, especially as a specialist in the rules of a language
core_image: 一个人在灯下俯身，把一句话逐词拆开，给每块贴上标签
scene: 一位研究语法的学者在灯下把一段长句拆成零件，逐一标上名称。The grammarian at the desk took the sentence apart and labelled each piece.
sceneCN: 这里 grammarian 是「语法学者」（第 1 个义项：研究语法的人）；句意：一位研究语法的学者在灯下把一段长句拆成零件，逐一标上名称。

pos.zh: 语法学家；语法专家；语法书作者

derivatives.zh: 语法；语法学，是 grammarian 的词基，去掉表人的后缀 -ian 即得
语法的；合乎语法的，由 grammar 加形容词后缀 -ical 构成
语法上；从语法角度看，由 grammatical 加副词后缀 -ly 构成

senses.title: A scholar of grammar
senses.definition: a person who studies the rules and structure of a language as a subject of research
senses.definitionCN: 把语言的规则与结构当作研究对象的人
senses.example: The grammarian spent years mapping the verb system of the old language.
senses.exampleCN: 这位语法学者花了多年时间梳理那门古语言的动词系统。
senses.why: Greek grammatikos named a person skilled in letters, so the word began as a label for someone expert in the written system of a language.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 grammatikos 指精通文字的人，所以这个词最初就是「精通一门语言书写体系者」的称号，研究者的含义由此而来。

senses.title: A writer of grammar books
senses.definition: a person who writes or compiles a grammar of a language, setting out its rules for learners
senses.definitionCN: 为学习者编写或整理某门语言语法规则的人
senses.example: A grammarian of the sixteenth century produced the first printed grammar of the dialect.
senses.exampleCN: 十六世纪的一位语法书作者编出了那门方言的第一部印刷语法。
senses.why: Medieval teachers needed written rules for pupils, and the person who drew them up took the name of the subject.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪的教师需要给学生写出规则，把这些规则整理成文的人便以学科之名得名。

senses.title: A teacher of grammar
senses.definition: in earlier use, a schoolmaster who taught Latin grammar and classical texts
senses.definitionCN: 较早用法中指教授拉丁语法与古典文本的教师
senses.example: In the old schools a grammarian taught Latin to boys for most of the day.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧式学校里，语法教师一天中大部分时间都在教男孩们拉丁语。
senses.why: Latin grammaticus also meant a schoolmaster, so for centuries the grammarian was simply the man at the front of the classroom.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 grammaticus 同时有教师之义，所以数百年间语法学家就是站在教室前面的那个人。

senses.title: A judge of correct usage
senses.definition: a person who states which forms of a language are correct, sometimes with more strictness than the language deserves
senses.definitionCN: 规定语言中哪些用法正确的人，有时严格得超出语言本身的实际情况
senses.example: The prescriptive grammarian condemned the split infinitive, though good writers used it freely.
senses.exampleCN: 这位规定主义语法学家斥责分裂不定式，尽管优秀作家一直自由地使用它。
senses.why: Once grammar was taught as a standard of correctness, the expert could turn into a judge who tells speakers what they may say.
senses.whyCN: 语法一旦被当作正确性的标准来教授，专家就可能变成裁决者，告诉说话人能说什么。

senses.title: A student of letters in the old sense
senses.definition: in older use, a scholar of classical languages and texts more broadly than the modern word suggests
senses.definitionCN: 较早用法中泛指研究古典语言与文献的学者，范围比现代用法更广
senses.example: Erasmus was praised as a grammarian before he was praised as a reformer.
senses.exampleCN: 伊拉斯谟先是以语文学者的身份受到称赞，后来才被称作改革者。
senses.why: Grammar once meant the whole of Latin letters, so a grammarian could be a scholar of the entire classical inheritance.
senses.whyCN: 语法之学曾经泛指整个拉丁文墨传统，所以语法学家可以是研究整份古典遗产的学者。

intro.en: Grammarian comes from Greek gramma, a letter, through Latin grammaticus, a grammarian or schoolmaster, and Old French gramarien.
intro.cn: grammarian 源自希腊语 gramma（字母），经拉丁语 grammaticus（语法学家、教师）与古法语 gramarien 进入英语。

items.en: Gramma means a letter or a written mark, and graphein means to write or draw.
items.cn: gramma 意为字母或写下的记号，graphein 意为写或画。

items.en: Grammatikos describes a person skilled in letters, and the word could also name such a person.
items.cn: grammatikos 形容精通文字的人，也可直接用来称呼这样的人。

items.en: Grammaticus means of grammar and also a grammarian or a schoolmaster.
items.cn: grammaticus 既表示「语法的」，也指语法学家或教师。

items.en: Gramarien names a person learned in Latin grammar.
items.cn: gramarien 指精通拉丁语法的人。

items.en: English grammarian first means a scholar of Latin, and later any student of grammar.
items.cn: 英语 grammarian 最初指拉丁文学者，后来泛指研究语法的人。

items.en: Modern English adds the prescriptive grammarian who judges usage.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了裁定用法对错的「规定主义语法学家」。

note.en: Grammarian belongs to the family of grammar and grammatical, and it sits beside the wider words for people who study language.
note.cn: grammarian 属于 grammar、grammatical 的词族，并与泛指研究语言之人的词相邻。

entries.definition: the rules by which words are put together into sentences
entries.definitionCN: 语法；把词组合成句子的规则

entries.definition: correct according to the rules of grammar
entries.definitionCN: 合乎语法的

entries.definition: in Britain, a secondary school that selects pupils by examination
entries.definitionCN: 英国的文法学校，即通过考试择优录取的中学

entries.definition: a person who studies language as a science
entries.definitionCN: 语言学家

entries.definition: a scholar who studies the history of languages and of written texts
entries.definitionCN: 语文学家；文献学家

entries.definition: a person who shows off detailed knowledge, especially about rules
entries.definitionCN: 卖弄学问的人；拘泥于规则的人

normalIntro.en: Grammarian is a transparent word: the subject grammar plus the person suffix -ian, with a Greek letter at the bottom of it.
normalIntro.cn: grammarian 是个透明的词：学科 grammar 加表人的后缀 -ian，最底下还压着一个希腊语的「字母」。

normal.en: Greek gramma, a letter, is the seed of grammar and of grammarian.
normal.cn: 希腊语 gramma（字母）是 grammar 与 grammarian 共同的种子。

normal.en: The suffix -ian marks a person, as in historian and musician.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ian 标记人，如 historian 与 musician 中的 -ian。

normal.en: A grammarian writes a grammar, and a grammar describes what a grammarian studies.
normal.cn: 语法学家写语法书，语法书描述的正是语法学家研究的东西。

normal.en: Prescriptive grammarian names the expert who lays down rules for others.
normal.cn: prescriptive grammarian 指为他人制定规则的那类专家。

normal.en: Compare linguist: a linguist studies language broadly, a grammarian concentrates on its rules.
normal.cn: 对比 linguist：语言学家广泛研究语言，语法学家专注其中的规则。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp at midnight and a long sentence copied out with every word tagged.
abstract.cn: 想象深夜的一盏灯，一句长话被抄下来，每个词都贴上了标签。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf of grammars with one author name repeated on the spines.
abstract.cn: 想象一排语法书，书脊上重复着同一个作者的名字。

abstract.en: Picture a schoolroom where a boy recites a Latin ending while the master listens.
abstract.cn: 想象一间教室，男孩背诵拉丁语词尾，老师在旁边听着。

examples.en: The grammarian argued that the two constructions carry different meanings.
examples.cn: 这位语法学家认为这两种结构含义不同。

examples.en: Grammarians have described the language for more than a century.
examples.cn: 语法学家研究并描写这门语言已有一百多年。

examples.en: A grammarian of the old school could quote Latin authors from memory.
examples.cn: 旧派的语法学家能凭记忆引用拉丁作家。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「格拉玛莲」——一位叫玛莲的女士捧着语法书，逐条讲解规则；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 gramma（字母）→ grammatikos（精通文字的人）→ 拉丁语 grammaticus（语法学家、教师）→ 古法语 gramarien → 英语 grammarian，核心是「与字母和规则打交道的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Grammarian begins with the expert in the written system of a language, then names the person who writes the rules down, the teacher who drills them, the judge who enforces them, and finally the old scholar of classical letters.
sensesIntro.cn: grammarian 从「精通一门语言书写体系的专家」开始，再指把规则写成书的人、训练学生的教师、裁定对错的评判者，最后指旧派研究古典文献的学者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person bent over a lamp, taking a sentence apart word by word.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人在灯下俯身，把一句话逐词拆开。

branches.en: The expert in the system is the central modern sense.
branches.cn: 精通这套体系的专家是核心的现代义项。

branches.en: The writer of grammars turns knowledge into a book.
branches.cn: 语法书的作者把知识变成一本书。

branches.en: The teacher carries the rules into the classroom.
branches.cn: 教师把规则带进课堂。

branches.en: The judge turns description into prescription.
branches.cn: 裁定者把描述变成规定。

branches.en: The old scholar and the modern expert both work through texts.
branches.cn: 旧派学者与现代专家都通过文本来工作。

intro.en: Grammarian is built from Greek gramma and the person suffix -ian, with Latin and French forms in between.
intro.cn: grammarian 由希腊语 gramma 与表人的后缀 -ian 构成，中间经过拉丁语与法语的形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin grammatica means grammar, and grammaticus means both skilled in grammar and a grammarian or schoolmaster.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 grammatica 意为语法，grammaticus 既指「精通语法的」，也指语法学家或教师。

items.example: Gramma is the first element of the family.
items.exampleCN: gramma 是这一词族的第一个元素。

items.example: Graphein lies behind gramma and graphic.
items.exampleCN: graphein 是 gramma 与 graphic 的更早来源。

items.example: Grammatikos passed into Latin almost unchanged.
items.exampleCN: grammatikos 几乎原样进入拉丁语。

items.example: Grammatica named the school subject.
items.exampleCN: grammatica 指学校里教的这门学科。

items.example: Grammaticus is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: grammaticus 是直接的拉丁语来源。

items.meaningCN: 法语中表示「与某事物相关的人」
items.example: Old French gramarien uses the suffix -ien.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 gramarien 用了后缀 -ien。

items.meaning: a person who works with or studies something
items.meaningCN: 表示从事或研究某事物的人
items.example: The suffix -ian forms grammarian.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ian 构成 grammarian。

items.example: Grammar is the subject the person studies.
items.exampleCN: grammar 是这个人所研究的学科。

items.meaning: relating to grammar, or correct by its rules
items.example: Grammatical keeps the adjective sense.
items.exampleCN: grammatical 保留了形容词义。

items.meaning: in a way that follows grammar
items.example: Grammatically judges how a sentence is built.
items.exampleCN: grammatically 用来评判句子构造得是否合规。

latinEntries.structure: Greek noun, source of Latin grammatica

definition_zh: 图形的；绘画的；计算机图形的；生动逼真的；露骨的；书写形式的；图像；图表
definition_en: relating to drawing or visual images, or described in such clear detail that the images are hard to forget
core_image: 铅笔在白纸上拉出一道看得见的线，画面替文字说话
scene: 车祸的报道写得过于细致，读的人几乎能看见现场。The report gave such a graphic account of the crash that readers could hardly finish it.
sceneCN: 这里 graphic 是「生动逼真的、露骨的」（第 4 个义项：细节清晰到令人不适）；句意：车祸的报道写得过于细致，读的人几乎能看见现场。

pos.zh: 图形的；绘画的；计算机图形的；生动逼真的；露骨的；书写形式的
图像；图表；图形

derivatives.zh: 形容词 graphic 加名词后缀 -ics，义为「图像；图形学」
graphic 加副词后缀 -ally，义为「以图形方式；生动地」
图表；曲线图，由希腊语同一词根缩略而来，与 graphic 同源

senses.title: Relating to drawing and design
senses.definition: connected with drawing, printing, or visual design rather than with words or sound
senses.definitionCN: 与绘画、印刷或视觉设计相关，而非与文字或声音相关
senses.example: She trained as a graphic artist before she turned to painting.
senses.exampleCN: 她在转去画画之前受训成为平面设计师。
senses.why: Greek graphikos meant skilled in drawing, so the first English sense simply named what belongs to drawing.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 graphikos 意为擅长绘画，所以英语最早的含义就是「属于绘画的」，视觉设计之义由此直接展开。

senses.title: A drawn picture or diagram
senses.definition: a picture, diagram, or design, especially one printed in a book or shown on a page
senses.definitionCN: 印在书上或页面上的一幅图画、图表或设计
senses.example: The report explains each step with a simple graphic.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告用一张简单的图表解释每一个步骤。
senses.why: A drawing is a graphic thing, and English turned the adjective into a noun for the object itself.
senses.whyCN: 一幅画本来就是「图形的」东西，英语便把这个形容词转为指物本身的名词，于是有了一幅图就是 a graphic 的说法。

senses.title: Made by a computer display
senses.definition: relating to images produced or shown by a computer, as in a graphic card or graphic software
senses.definitionCN: 与计算机生成或显示的图像相关，如显卡或图形软件
senses.example: The game needs a faster graphic card to run smoothly.
senses.exampleCN: 这个游戏需要更快的显卡才能流畅运行。
senses.why: Computing reused the drawing sense for pictures made of pixels, so a graphic card is literally a drawing card for the machine.
senses.whyCN: 计算机把「绘画」义借去指由像素拼成的画面，于是显卡字面上就是机器的绘画卡。

senses.title: Vivid and unpleasantly clear
senses.titleCN: 生动得令人不适的；露骨的
senses.definition: described in such clear detail that the images are hard to forget, often because the subject is shocking
senses.definitionCN: 描写细致清晰到让人难以忘记，常因内容骇人
senses.example: The witness gave a graphic description of the injuries.
senses.exampleCN: 证人详详细细地描述了那些伤情，听者难以忘记。
senses.why: From a picture that is true to life comes the sense of words that draw a picture, and such pictures can be too sharp.
senses.whyCN: 从「逼真的画」引申出「文字画出一幅画」的用法，而这种画面有时过于锐利，令人不适。

senses.title: Written rather than spoken
senses.definition: of a sign or symbol, written or drawn instead of spoken
senses.definitionCN: 指符号或标记以书写或绘制形式出现，而非口头说出
senses.example: The dictionary lists the graphic form of each word beside its pronunciation.
senses.exampleCN: 词典在每个词的读音旁边列出它的书写形式。
senses.why: The root covers both writing and drawing, so graphic can set written symbols against spoken sound.
senses.whyCN: 这个词根同时覆盖「写」与「画」，所以 graphic 可以把书面符号与口头发音对立起来。

intro.en: Graphic comes from Greek graphikos, of drawing or writing, through Latin graphicus, and entered English in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: graphic 源自希腊语 graphikos（绘画或书写的），经拉丁语 graphicus 进入英语，首见于十七世纪。

items.en: Graphein means to write, draw, or scratch, and graphe means a drawing or a writing.
items.cn: graphein 意为写、画或刻，graphe 意为图画或文字。

items.en: Graphikos means of drawing or writing, and also able to draw.
items.cn: graphikos 意为绘画或书写的，也指善于绘画的。

items.en: Graphicus keeps the sense of painting and drawing, and is used of a finely drawn style.
items.cn: graphicus 保留绘画与描画之义，也用于形容描画精细的文风。

items.en: Graphic first means of drawing or painting, then vivid, like a picture drawn in words.
items.cn: graphic 最初指绘画的，随后指像用文字画出一幅画那样生动。

items.en: Modern English adds graphic design, graphics as pictures, and computer graphics.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了 graphic design、表示图像的 graphics 以及 computer graphics。

note.en: Graphic shares the Greek root of writing and drawing with graph and grapheme, and it sits beside the words for clear description and for things seen.
note.cn: graphic 与 graph、grapheme 共享希腊语「写、画」词根，并与表示清晰描写和视觉事物的词相邻。

entries.definition: a diagram that shows how two quantities are related
entries.definitionCN: 图表；曲线图，与 graphic 同出希腊语「写、画」词根

entries.definition: pictures and designs, especially ones shown on a computer screen
entries.definitionCN: 图形；图像，尤指屏幕上的图像

entries.definition: the smallest written unit of a language, such as a letter
entries.definitionCN: 字素；书写的最小单位，如一个字母

entries.definition: producing strong, clear images in the mind
entries.definitionCN: 生动的；鲜明的

entries.definition: stated clearly and in detail, leaving nothing implied
entries.definitionCN: 明确的；直白露骨的

entries.definition: relating to sight or to things that are seen
entries.definitionCN: 视觉的；看得见的

normalIntro.en: Graphic keeps the Greek verb for scratching a mark into a surface, so drawing and writing are one idea in this word.
normalIntro.cn: graphic 保留着希腊语「在表面上刻下记号」的动词，所以在这个词里，画与写是同一件事。

normal.en: Greek graphein, to write or draw, also hides inside photograph and geography.
normal.cn: 希腊语 graphein（写、画）也藏在 photograph 与 geography 里面。

normal.en: The suffix -ic turns the root into an adjective: graphic means of drawing.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ic 把词根变成形容词：graphic 意为绘画的。

normal.en: Graphic detail draws a picture in words; graphic violence does the same with shocks.
normal.cn: graphic detail 用文字作画，graphic violence 则用冲击性的画面作画。

normal.en: Graphics is the plural noun for pictures, especially on a screen.
normal.cn: graphics 是表示图像的名词复数形式，尤指屏幕上的图像。

normal.en: Compare vivid: vivid can be pleasant, while graphic often warns that the detail is uncomfortable.
normal.cn: 对比 vivid：vivid 可以是愉快的，而 graphic 常暗示细节令人不适。

abstract.en: Picture a pencil tracing a curve until the shape stands out from the paper.
abstract.cn: 想象铅笔描出一条曲线，直到形状从纸上立起来。

abstract.en: Picture a framed diagram on a page, with arrows and boxes doing the talking.
abstract.cn: 想象页面上一个装框的图表，箭头和方框替人说话。

abstract.en: Picture a screen lighting up with polygons that move like water.
abstract.cn: 想象屏幕亮起，多边形像水一样流动。

examples.en: She studied graphic design before she became an illustrator.
examples.cn: 她在成为插画家之前学的是平面设计。

examples.en: The documentary is graphic in its account of the flood.
examples.cn: 这部纪录片对洪水的叙述细致得令人不忍。

examples.en: The graphics on the old console still look charming.
examples.cn: 那台旧游戏机上的画面今天看仍然讨人喜欢。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「格拉菲克」——一位画家把颜色刻进纸里，画面清楚得让人不敢细看；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 graphein（写、画）→ graphe（图画、文字）→ graphikos（绘画的）→ 拉丁语 graphicus → 英语 graphic，核心是「用线条留下痕迹」。

sensesIntro.en: Graphic moves from the act of drawing to the drawn object, then to machine-made pictures, and finally to words that draw too sharp a picture.
sensesIntro.cn: graphic 从绘画这个动作，转到画出来的东西，再转到机器生成的图像，最后转到把画面画得过于清晰的文字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pencil pulling a visible line across white paper.
core.cn: 核心意象：铅笔在白纸上拉出一道看得见的线。

branches.en: What belongs to drawing is the oldest English sense.
branches.cn: 属于绘画的事物是英语中最古老的义项。

branches.en: The adjective turns into a noun for the drawn object.
branches.cn: 形容词转为指画出来之物的名词。

branches.en: The drawing sense is borrowed for machine-made pictures.
branches.cn: 绘画义被借去指机器生成的图像。

branches.en: Words that draw a picture too sharply become graphic in tone.
branches.cn: 把画面画得过于锐利的文字，语气上就成了 graphic。

branches.en: Drawing and writing share the root, so graphic can mean written rather than spoken.
branches.cn: 画与写共享同一个词根，所以 graphic 可以表示书写的而非口说的。

intro.en: Graphic is built on the Greek root graph, write or draw, with the adjective suffix -ic and the noun suffix -ics around it.
intro.cn: graphic 建立在希腊语词根 graph（写、画）之上，周围有形容词后缀 -ic 与名词后缀 -ics。

latinIntro.en: Latin graphicus, borrowed from Greek graphikos, means of painting or drawing and describes a finely drawn style.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 graphicus 借自希腊语 graphikos，意为绘画的，也形容描画精细的风格。

items.example: The root graph carries the idea of a mark made by hand.
items.exampleCN: 词根 graph 承载「手留下的痕迹」这一概念。

items.example: Graphein is the verb behind the root.
items.exampleCN: graphein 是这个词根背后的动词。

items.example: Graphe names the thing produced.
items.exampleCN: graphe 指被制作出来的东西。

items.example: Graphikos describes what belongs to drawing.
items.exampleCN: graphikos 描述属于绘画的事物。

items.example: Graphicus carries the word into Latin.
items.exampleCN: graphicus 把这个词带进拉丁语。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms graphic.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ic 构成 graphic。

items.example: Graphic keeps both senses in English.
items.exampleCN: graphic 在英语中保留了两重含义。

items.meaning: a field of study or a set of things
items.meaningCN: 表示学科或事物集合的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ics forms graphics.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ics 构成 graphics。

items.example: Graphics names the pictures themselves.
items.exampleCN: graphics 指图像本身。

items.meaning: by means of a drawing, or in vivid detail
items.example: Graphically extends the adjective.
items.exampleCN: graphically 是形容词的副词扩展。

latinEntries.meaning: of painting or drawing, finely drawn
